Title: Jungle Safari
Teaser: Put on your safari gear and embark on an incredible and memorable journey through the deepest, darkest regions of the jungle.
Description:
Put on your safari gear and embark on an incredible and memorable journey through the deepest, darkest regions of the jungle. Our team will help you discover the fascinating world of animal communication and learn more about the amazing range of sounds the creatures of the jungle make.

Please note: this workshop is closed with no viewing area for parents.

Title: James Van Praagh
Description: New York Times best-selling author and subject of a major Hollywood film starring Ted Danson, James Van Praagh demonstrates his unique talent and psychic abilities in a demonstration of communication from the unseen world! James is one of America's best known psychics. Star of film and TV and award-winning author brings his show to the Fringe for the first time. James usually fills large stadia, so this is a unique opportunity to see one of the best in the world demonstrate his skills up close and personal, in this intimate venue in Edinburgh.
Venue description: Victorian townhouse.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Two steps into the building from pavement level

Title: Happy Hour with InChorus
Description: Happy Hour with InChorus. This large contemporary choir performs an intoxicating cocktail of popular songs in an exciting blend of arrangements. A polished performance served with undiluted spirit and zest, this is the perfect entertainment aperitif to your Fringe evening. InChorus is a large vibrant choir from Peebles. Formed in 2008, they have twice filled the Festival Theatre and Usher Hall. In 2011 they were asked to perform in New York for the 10th anniversary commemorations of 9/11. This is their second Festival Fringe experience, having sung to a sell-out audience at St Augustine’s in 2013.
Venue description: After its phenomenally successful launch in 2014 Greenside @ Nicolson Square is back in 2015. Set in the heart of town, seconds from the BBC@Potterow, the internationally renowned Festival Theatre and the hustle and bustle of the Royal Mile. We’re bringing our desire for creating great spaces and passion for service to the heart of the festival.
Venue accessibility: Venue underwent a full multi-million pound refurbishment in 2013 making the whole site accessible. Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Graham Clark Reads the Phonebook
Description: In an era where the phone book is going extinct, Graham Clark Reads the Phonebook serves as a fitting eulogy to the tome everyone used to own. Clark will leave no stone unturned while focusing his observational lens on the subject at hand.
Artist: Graham Clark produced by the Pajama Men
Venue description: Assembly George Square Studios are located opposite the entrance to Assembly George Square Gardens and next to Assembly George Square Theatre. The Studios have some of the best audience facilities on the Fringe. All five Studios have comfortable modern seating, and the modern indoor Studios Bar has plenty of sofas, a much used piano and serves freshly prepared hot and cold meals.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Joy is the Enemy of Progress
Description: Are you happy? No, of course not. You’re not supposed to be. The only human beings who're truly happy sit around the war memorial drinking shoe polish. Forget trying to be being happy, embrace the misery and try to enjoy the simple things in life, such as an hour of unpretentious, brutally honest stand-up comedy that's way better than you think it’s going to be. ‘He sees that thin line, and he runs towards it at full speed, but stops in just time to avoid seriously getting anyone’s nose out of joint’ **** (ViewsFromTheGods.co.uk).
Venue: Just the Tonic at the Caves (Salvation Rooms)
Venue description: Just the Tonic Fringe venue right next to the Caves.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. It has a cobbled street leading to the entrance

Title: Dan Lees: Brainchild
Description: Life's weightier questions are thoroughly demolished in Dan Lees' Brainchild, an award-winning physical comedy that veers from the profound to the ridiculous. A host of bizarre characters explore the futility of our existence, from a cheese-loving Pope to a lonely cowboy with only a goldfish for a friend. Directed by Mick Barnfather (Complicite, Told By An Idiot). 'An evening of discovery and laughter' **** (Adelaide Advertiser). 'Downright hilarious ... comedy that deserves to be commended for challenging the boundaries and creating an unforgettable experience' **** (BroadwayBaby.com). Judges Award for Theatre winner, Mimetic Festival 2014.
Venue description: Situated at the heart of the festival, between George Square and Teviot Place, the Med Quad is where you can find venues Ermintrude, Daisy and Clover, presenting theatre, comedy, cabaret and family shows early til late.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: The Tobolowsky Files
Description: Hollywood character actor Stephen Tobolowsky shares some of his hilarious, moving, and profound stories about life, love and the entertainment industry. The Tobolowsky Files has been a podcast sensation since 2009, and now he brings his wild and crazy adventures to Edinburgh for the first time. Find out what happened when he was held hostage at gunpoint, broke his neck in five places while horseback riding in Iceland, his experiences as an accidental drug dealer, and when he inadvertently coined the name of a famous British rock band.
Venue description: Soak up the legendary atmosphere at the Pleasance Courtyard, considered by many to be the heart of the Fringe. With every entertainment under the sun in seventeen venues, come take in a show, enjoy a drink and stay for the day. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).
Venue accessibility: A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Spring Awakening
Description: An exhilarating electrifying fusion of morality, sexuality and rock’n’roll, Spring Awakening is an edgy, rock musical adaptation of the seminal play about the trials and tribulations of growing up. Winner of eight Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Spring Awakening explores the journey from adolescence to adulthood with poignancy and passion that is both illuminating and unforgettable. ‘Rousing rock songs ... Worked perfectly ... Impressive vocals from all the cast ... A thoroughly enjoyable performance ... The audience seemed enraptured’ (ThreeWeeks, Spring Awakening, 2012).
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.
Venue description: A fabulous Magic Mirror tent, has arrived this year for greater spiegel experiences! The Famous Spiegeltent, an iconic mainstay of The Edinburgh Festival and a star in her own right, hosts a myriad of stunning performances. Since Marlene Dietrich sang Falling in Love Again on the stage in the 1930’s, her magic mirrors have reflected thousands of artists, audiences and exotic gatherings. Welcome to the world of The Famous Spiegeltent.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Ada
Description: An enchantress of numbers, Ada Lovelace was a mathematician, a celebrity, a poetical scientist, the daughter of Lord Byron and the world’s first computer programmer. Using the structure of a computer algorithm, Ada explores the link between technology and creativity and the continued impact of her work today. This is an inventive, playful and powerful new devised show that brings the inspirational achievements and legacy of Ada Lovelace to life, created on the 200th anniversary of her birth.
Venue description: A unique theatre in a converted church in the heart of Edinburgh, Bedlam Theatre returns to the Fringe for its 35th year with another exciting and eclectic programme of theatre and comedy.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking

Title: April the Red Goldfish with Marjolaine Leray
Description: Join author and illustrator Marjolaine Leray and her translator Sarah Ardizzone for a fun-filled hour of stories, drawing and translation. Marjolaine will introduce April the Red Goldfish, a quirky, humorous picture book full of jokes that can sometimes be a challenge to translate! Perfect for anyone who loves to see how stories evolve and for any budding linguists or bilinguals.

Title: Chap at the Door and The Aftermath
Description: Behind every person misusing substances is a family. Chap at the Door and The Aftermath is a unique family written and performed two-part illustration providing a family perspective on the impact of substance misuse. The heart-wrenching perspectives provide insight into the sacrifice, loss, struggles and hope families encounter in their battle with addiction. They highlight issues families face following a drug-related death, raise awareness of support, fight stigma and promote the use of naloxone – the overdose reversal drug.
Artist: Scottish Families Affected by Alcohol & Drugs and FASS
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hotel), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.
Venue accessibility: Level access on ground floor. Lift access to Lindisfarne Room. No wheelchair access to gallery. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, Reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Vehicular access is via churchyard entrance on King's Stables Road

Title: Sing in the City Concert for When You Wish Upon a Star
Description: For one night only, Sing in The City’s premier choir The Aw’ Blacks will be performing in this year’s Edinburgh Fringe. Previous years have been sell-outs and from the first notes you will be enraptured by this stunning contemporary choir. For young and old, one of the best musical performances you will see in the Festival this year! All proceeds will go to Wishes for Scottish Children suffering from a life-threatening illness.
Venue: St Andrew's and St George's West, George St
Venue description: A beautiful, easily accessible 18th century New Town church, which hosts a variety of musical performances - from soloists to choirs, instrumentalists to small orchestras and bands in all musical genres: classical, folk, jazz, songs from the shows, opera, world music.  Enjoy light lunches and snacks in the Undercroft cafe, or sit and admire the newly refurbished building.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Lift access to cafe and toilets

Title: Neel Kolhatkar: Truth Be Told
Description: After sell-out solo shows and tours across Australia Neel returns for his second Edinburgh solo outing with Truth Be Told. Neel makes astute social and cultural observations while displaying flawless characterisations and voices, charismatic delivery and a sharp wit. There is a reason he has over half a million followers across social media – do not miss this rising star of Australian comedy. 'Hilarious throughout, thought-provoking and very well written' (YAWP). 'Neel kept the audience laughing throughout one hour of hilarity with his impressively wide-ranging impressions' (Fresh Air, Edinburgh). ‘Brilliant’ (Sydney Morning Herald).
Warnings: Strong language
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces and seven bars including the exclusive roof top bar, The Loft. A must for all Fringe-goers. A massive mini-Fringe under one roof, this iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe! All spaces, the café and all seven bars are wheelchair accessible, with the exception of the Balcony and Billiard Rooms. Tickets available 24-hours online!
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The building is accessed by 8 steps or an external wheelchair lift

Title: A Half of Innes - Neil Innes in Conversation
Description:
Following the last-minute cancellation of The Rutles: All You Need is Cash, due to complicated and unusual rights issues, EIFF is proud to offer you A Half of Innes. Join us for this in-person discussion about the making of the fantastic film you won't see, featuring the man who fronted the legendary band you won't hear, and who wrote and recorded the vital, timeless soundtrack you won't experience in any other sensory shape or form: the multi-talented musician and performer, Mr Neil Innes.
EIFF's Little Big Screen strand is supported by American Airlines.

Title: Meet and Greet for University Students
Description: Are you a university student at the Fringe? Network with your tech, acting, management and producing peers – make connections! Come meet other university students at this meet and greet sponsored by Fringe University.
Venue description: Summerhall presents engaging, challenging, high-quality theatre, dance, literature, visual art and music for people of all ages.  Our unique home in the former Dick Vet building of the University of Edinburgh offers atmospheric performance spaces, a buzzy courtyard and an onsite pub, the Royal Dick Bar, with something for everyone to explore, discover and enjoy - “an entire festival in its own right” The Guardian
Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café.
We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please do not hesitate to contact us by phone on 0845 874 3000 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

http://www.summerhall.co.uk/about/accessibility/. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Ramp access is at the side of the venue on Summerhall Square.

Title: Oh It's That Guy! Comedian Matt Henry
Description: The good times are here! The Canadian Rasta is back in Edinburgh once again. Settle in for some serious laughs.
Artist: CMH Originals Presents: Oh It's That Guy!
Venue description: Former retail space directly off the pavement in a great location.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: The Inquest
Teaser: Should Robert Knox have been tried with Burke and Hare? The decision is yours...
Description: Join the Inquest! We're taking you back to 1829 and an unidentified person has been found at Surgeons' Hall. Without any obvious cause of death, curator Robert Knox is finally called into question. Examine the scene of the crime, explore contemporary medical texts and illustrations, and discover the good and bad sides of Robert Knox. Should Robert Knox have been tried with Burke and Hare? The decision is yours...

Title: Music of Two Nations
Description: Eddie McGuire, former Chairman of the Musicians’ Union (Scottish Region), and classical zheng performer Dong Yi, the first and so far only musician of any Chinese instrument to give a public recital in China's Great Hall of the People, are celebrating the 10th year of their collaboration by giving a presentation with bamboo flutes, classical flutes and Chinese zheng (zither) with a recorded history of over 2,500 years and 36,000,000 active participants, on the music of the two nations in comparative perspective. Part of the Sixth Glamour of Jasmine Chinese arts festival.
Venue: St Andrew's and St George's West, George St
Venue description: A beautiful, easily accessible 18th century New Town church, which hosts a variety of musical performances - from soloists to choirs, instrumentalists to small orchestras and bands in all musical genres: classical, folk, jazz, songs from the shows, opera, world music.  Enjoy light lunches and snacks in the Undercroft cafe, or sit and admire the newly refurbished building.

Title: Shaggers
Description: The worldwide hit show returns with a line-up of superb and varied comedians from all around the Fringe doing material based around the hilarious, cheeky subject of shagging. ‘A tour de force of laughter filled mischievous comedy’ ***** (ArtsInLeicestershire.co.uk). ‘Excellent’ ***** (Audience Review, Edfringe.com). ‘Utterly hilarious’ ****1/2 (Perth Fringe World). ‘Possibly the best value show at the Festival’ **** (Herald Sun, Melbourne).
Venue description: Edinburgh's flagship free venue, located right in the centre of Edinburgh, with free shows running from 12:00-05:00 every day in four rooms. With five stylish bars open all day, and a free nightclub from 21:00-05:00.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking

Title: Five Drinks
Description: Five Drinks is an original play about the unique experience of gay dating. Dylan is on a drinks date with Archie but recalls a series of drinks in which he learns how to date, who to date, and the limitations of one’s own personal progress. It’s a comparison of different journeys towards a gay identity, a reverse exploration of a move between experience and innocence of an entire adult world. This is a story of Dylan Moon; his experience of being underwhelmed by others, understood by himself, and surprised by time.
Venue description: Paradise Green is the heart and soul of the largest arts festival in the world, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, relax with a drink from our snack bar before your performance and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Oh Hello!
Description: Charles Hawtrey was one of the leading lights of the Carry On film franchise, but as his career waned so his behaviour became more drunken and eccentric. See him in this one-man show as he regales stories of 50 years in the film industry, working with the likes of Alfred Hitchcock. Hear of his hilarious run-ins with Kenneth Williams, his disdain of the Carry On film producers as well as his complex relationship with his senile mother. Written by Dave Ainsworth and produced by the Torch Theatre Company in the centenary year of Hawtrey's birth.
Venue description: The magnificent venue atop the Mound is the most prestigious venue on the Fringe and hosts the finest drama, music and comedy. Entrance and box office through New College Quad off Mound Place. The venue houses three spaces; the Main Hall, Rainy Hall and Baillie Room.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Assembly Hall is on Mound Place up a steep hill. Box Office and Bar has step free access, but there is a large steep flight of steps up to the venues from this entrance. Baillie Room is not accessible, but the Main Hall and Rainy Hall have wheelchair access via a rear entrance on Lawn Market - please arrange access in advance and arrive a full 30 minutes before show time if wheelchair or step free access to either Main Hall or Rainy Hall is required. Call 0131 510 5539 for assistant venue

Title: Edinburgh Bhangra Crew
Description:
The Edinburgh Bhangra Crew are a non-profit university dance troupe founded in 2008 by a small group of friends who love to dance. Bhangra, a celebratory Punjabi folk dance, has taught to the group in open classes twice a week and since its founding.  Since the group’s inception, Edinburgh Bhangra Crew have gone from strength to strength and now boast over 60 members!

They have danced at a range of events from local charity performances, weddings, and dance shows up to national Bhangra competitions, and continue to deliver lively and colourful performances.  The Edinburgh Bhangra Crew are a firm festival favourite – bringing colour and energy to our World Dance Feste Stage.

Part of a full day programme of events - ticket prices are per day. Free entry for children under 12. Timings subject to change.
Venue address:
Leith Links
Opposite Duncan Place
Edinburgh
Venue accessibility:
The site is fully accessible, although it must be noted that the festival is an outdoor event on a largely grass surface. Accessible toilets will be provided and assistance will be available for disabled patrons at the box office and the site entrance.
A very limited number of parking spaces will be available for disabled visitors in the production carpark just off John's Place

Title: John Lister-Kaye
Subtitle: At One With Nature
Description: For over 30 years, naturalist and conservationist Sir John Lister-Kaye has been observing the spectacular seasonal metamorphosis at the Aigas Field Centre in the Highlands. His new book, Gods of the Morning, is an affectionate look at the birdlife which occupies the territory as he wonders whether we are losing touch with the natural world.

Title: Australia is F*cked
Description: Kieran Butler **** (Scotsman) returns with an updated version of his political comedy/satire. In 2013/14, capacity crowds saw Butler lampoon the myopic psyche that the current Australian government has since put on display for the world. Butler’s predictions over the past few years have been alarmingly accurate. He recently predicted PM Tony Abbott would stage an electoral comeback by going ‘full racist’. This is stand-up and musical comedy that proves why Australia is the joke everyone else is completely sick and tired of. Australia: We will kill your dogs if you don’t follow proper procedure.
Venue description: Holding

Title: Anna Morris: It's Got To Be Perfect
Description: The critically acclaimed character comic, star of ITV2's Bad Bridesmaid and BBC One's Outnumbered, returns after the success of last year’s sell-out hit show, Would Like to Thank. Georgina (of Morris’s viral YouTube series Georgina’s Wedding Blogs) is getting married in Edinburgh and it’s got to be perfect. She’s having 22 rehearsals first, during the festival, and you are invited! ‘Spot-on, darkly comic characters. She’s comedy gold’ (HuffingtonPost.co.uk). ‘Beautifully crafted comedy’ (Independent). ‘An exceptional comedy performer’ **** (Skinny). **** (Stage). **** (Herald). **** (Broadway Baby). **** (Sunday Herald). **** (One4Review.co.uk).
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award-winning entertainment venue with cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860's interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy, ballroom and space 3 will be used during the festival. 18+age restriction. www.thevoodoorooms.com

Title: Bereave
Description: Garvey (Malcolm McDowell) has a secret and a gun. his wife, Evelyn (Jane Seymour), has a sword and a glass of wine. Garvey’s brother, victor (Keith Carradine), has a really terrible haircut, but that’s incidental. Are they okay? They’re fine, thank you for asking. Why wouldn’t they be fine? They’ve got secrets and guns and swords and glasses of wine and really terrible haircuts. See this film, draw your own conclusions and get a trim.

Title: Virgin Money Fringe on the Royal Mile
Description: Watch free previews of hundreds of Fringe shows. See world-class street performers, buskers and entertainers of every talent imaginable perform daily on Edinburgh's historic Royal Mile. Daily schedule available at www.edfringe.com/streetevents.
Artist: Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society / Virgin Money Street Events
Venue: High Street, Cockburn Street to George IV Bridge
Venue description: The High Street is transformed into a huge performance space for all to enjoy. World-class street performers, buskers, an arts and craft market, the Fringe box office and millions of flyers make this the centre of the Edinburgh Festival Fringe.

Title: Sharma Sharma Sharma Sharma Sharma Comedian!
Description: Mickey is an Indian, that was born in Pakistan (it’s true). After living in Karachi, Beijing, Hong Kong, New Delhi and Kashmir ... Mickey ended up in the exotic climes of Birmingham at the age of 19. Watch Mickey's evolution from an Indian immigrant into a British comic.
Venue description: A fashionable newly refurbished cafe-bar right in the centre of town, between the Royal Mile and Cowgate, open daily for food and drink. With a section of free Fringe shows in the downstairs room throughout the day.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking

Title: How to Sell Your Show
Description: Meet PR and media insiders: tips on everything from social networking and contacting reviewers to increasing audience numbers. Led by the Fringe Society's media office, this discussion will give you invaluable advice on marketing your show at the festival. Panellists will be announced through media office e-bulletins and on Twitter through @fringecentral.
Venue description:
Fringe Central is a resource developed for participants providing support, free events, and a centralised hub for professional development
opportunities.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There are two sets of approximately 10 steps up to the entrance of Fringe Central. The disabled access route is through the back of the building, via Chapel Street

Title: Squish Squared
Description: Dance and squash collide in Squish Squared, an energetic and humorous look at the spirit of competition. Created for the Glasgow 2014 Cultural Programme, Squish Squared takes place within glass backed squash courts. Audiences view the action through the glass and are then invited to have a go at bashing a ball against a wall. A contemporary dance male duet, the show revolves around the theme of one-upmanship between our two protagonists. Ultimately they discover that, despite their differences, they are both competing for the same thing and may have to work together to achieve that goal.
Venue description: A beautiful private squash club hosting a very special site specific performance by Room 2 Manoeuvre.

Title: Guitarray
Description: To celebrate his 20th Festival, Luca Villani plays a formidable array of the most beautiful compositions of his wide guitar repertoire. Starting with Fernando Sor’s Scottish Fantasy, followed by J.S.Bach famous Sarabande and Gavotte. Then great Romantic age hits: Albèniz’s Torre Bermeja and Asturias, Tarrega’s Recuerdos de la Alhambra. Barrios virtuosity will be represented by the poignant La Catedral, while Villa-Lobos brazilian mood by Study no 7 and the popular Choros no 1. A happy ending will be warranted by the flamboyant Fandango by Joaquin  Rodrigo. Four centuries of music in one hour of sheer beauty and emotion.

Title: Scotland In Six Swallies
Description: A river of drink runs through Scotland’s history – plague, murder, temperance and social reform are drenched in six iconic drinks (swallies, as the locals say). Alcohol is involved. Dangerous ideas and Susan Morrison lurk everywhere. This will not be entirely serious. Tea reviving Suffragettes and temperance women, coffee fuelling late night Enlightenment argy-bargy, burgundy spilling from goblets dropped by murdered royalty, whisky pouring into Prohibition America, Irn Bru baffling tourists trying to work out what that taste actually is, and water, the suspect carrier of disease and bringer of massive change to our cities.

Struggling with his feelings, Ken looks to build a new relationship with the streetwise yet vulnerable Helen, with tragic consequences. Dealing with real and current issues the play takes us on an emotional journey that is hard-hitting, though-provoking and tender, allowing us to question our ideas and beliefs. Egypt-born, RADA-trained, allergic to conventionality, Ross became a respected political journalist and single-handedly raised a daughter who herself overturned convention. Ross was also the muse for a Hollywood-bound German pianist, and of the lyricist Eric Maschwitz – his song These Foolish Things, written about Ross, is among the authentic songs featured in the production.

This event features the work of Roxana Vilk, the Iranian filmmaker, and the Qisetna: Talking Syria blog, as well as recent literature featuring the distinctive experiences that defy stereotypes and preconceptions to touch our humanity.

Title: Yasmin Alibhai-Brown: Promiscuous England
Description: The English have been typecast as imperial snobs, rule-bound, repressed, class-ridden, prejudiced – their racism cuts and scars. But reel through their long history to now and you find they can be passionate, wanton, infinitely curious and open. More so than hot blooded Mediterranean and Eastern peoples, or the other UK tribes. Their national dish is curry and their saint is from Syria, with skin as brown as mine. That story needs to be reclaimed and told, most of all to those who are drawn to Ukip and narrow nationalism.

Now, in a thought-provoking book, How the World Was Won, he charts the rise of the United States after 1945 to become ‘master of everything’, winning over the world with jeans, candy bars and captivating film icons. But is America’s influence waning? Chaired by Sheena McDonald.

Title: Hamlet (A One Man Play)
Description: Hamlet (A One Man Play) is a work of theatrical research where the only limit is the text. The actor explores all the possibilities, restructuring the original order of the fable. ‘There was truth in every character he played’ (Carla Capeáns, TeatroGalego.com). ‘Alfredo Padilla is giving to us a real art lesson on the stage inspired by Thalia’ (Alfredo Conde, Spanish National literature Award). ‘In one naked scenario Alfredo keeps the flight so high. Each and every feeling on the stage’ (Fernando Llorente, Diario Montañés). Winner of Best Actor at Carabanchel Festival, Madrid. www.alfredopadilla.es

Our central, easy to find venue, 40m from Princes Street, presents an outstanding programme of international companies, interactive children's theatre, drama workshops, innovative plays, musicals, dance, music, magic, poetry, comedy and cabaret. Spotlites has a repuation for quality five and four star sell-outs, clean facilities and caring, helpful staff.

Title: Seymour Stiffs – The Undertaker
Description: Seymour Stiffs, The Undertaker, invites you into his chapel of unrest. From out of the darkness this minister of mirth, mayhem and merriment emerges. Seymour delights in mocking, shocking and provoking mischievous thoughts about life and death. I am the jester, joker, the dark provoker. Seymour is energetic, physical and immersive. Out of seven billion people on this planet there is only one you, make your life count, live your life not someone else’s. No one show is ever the same. 'Dead funny, highly humorous, cleverly scripted, this was comedy at its best’ (Stratford Herald).
Warnings: Some strong language

Title: Puppet Fiction
Description: Everybody be cool! This is a mother f*cking puppet show! The ultimate Tarantino homage, this is Pulp Fiction with strings attached, literally. Award-winning hit show from New Zealand, three performers, 17 marionettes, three episodes, one hour of bat-sh*t crazy madness! An instant cult hit, Puppet Fiction has played in festivals around New Zealand and Australia and now puppet maker Jon Coddington's remarkable creation comes to Edinburgh. Come once for a slice or three times for the whole pie! ‘Fresh and funny’ (Sydney Morning Herald). ‘…pure comedy genius’ (AussieTheatre.com).

Title: Give Me a Reason to Live
Description: Inspired by the work of medieval painter Hieronymus Bosch, this stark solo explores issues of religion, religious art, judgement of bodies and quality of life. Taking the form of a series of tests, of body and of faith, and set to a mesmerising sound score, the work is a study in empathy; a live memorial to the disabled victims of the Nazi euthanasia program and the current disabled victims of the present UK government's so-called welfare reform. 'Stark (and) brutal with her customary integrity and conviction' **** (Herald). www.madeinscotlandshowcase.com.

Title: Knowledge and a Girl
Description: Howard Barker twists Grimm's Little Snow White into a spiky fable. 'I sleep with seven men,' she says. There are no innocent maidens or wicked stepmothers here, only women seeking enlightenment through erotic transgression. Barker delves into the intricacies of sexual maturity, explodes contemporary obsessions with youthfulness, and exposes how women are punished for a visible sexuality. But there's no social realism here – this is a truly Grimm world of mirrors, where the Queen's punishment is taken to the fairytale extreme, where the cost of desire and its knowledge is paid in blood. UK premiere.

Description: Sexy, spectacular, sparkling (and a little sadomasochistic). Velvet completely redefines cabaret as a disco inferno that shocks, surprises, scintillates at every turn. A party – funky, fresh, fun, sexy. The must-see show of the Fringe! Astonishing hit of the Adelaide Fringe 2015. An electrifying trip to a world of glamour and abandon including vocal, dance and acrobatic stars. Leaves the audience stunned and awestruck. A fantastic experience of sensory overload that gets not only a standing but boogying ovation. This is a stunner of a show, nothing but an endorphin rush! www.velvettheshow.com

Description: Learn about the internal, external and physical blocks that prevent you from delivering your best onstage performance. This interactive workshop draws on philosophical, psychological and body/mind teachings and research, delivering practical solutions for musicians and singers. Workshop is facilitated by professional singer/actor/musician/teacher Melissa Western, based on a decade of research and teaching at tertiary level. You will take away a full set of resources to continue on the journey of improving your stagecraft. Invest one short hour of your time this Fringe to nurturing and improving your craft – you won't regret it!

Title: Bernard O'Donoghue
Subtitle: Chaucer: The Father of English Literature
Description: For nearly two decades before his death in 1400, Geoffrey Chaucer toiled away at his epochal The Canterbury Tales, wholly unaware that he would inspire later generations of writers including Shakespeare, Austen and Dickens. In his new book, Whitbread Award-winning poet and medievalist Bernard O’Donoghue analyses Chaucer’s poems, explaining why his work captures the character of its era and has inspired writers ever since. Chaired by James Runcie.

Title: The Witch of Edmonton
Description: Edmonton: such an idyllic village. Mother Sawyer, a poor and lonely old woman, has turned to the devil to revenge herself on the village that called her, what else but, a witch. Well-loved Frank, on the other hand, has secretly become a bigamist in order to protect his family’s fortunes. As Sawyer’s familiar, a black dog from hell, torments the villagers and an elopement ends in murder, the people of Edmonton must decide what merits forgiveness when everyone is to blame. Multi award-winning EGTG present this rarely performed Jacobean play.

Title: Mark Thompson's A Space Traveller's Guide to the Solar System
Description: Is it possible for one person to journey around the solar system in the space of a human lifetime? This show is as much about the alien worlds in our planetary neighborhood as it is about the experience of travelling in space. Mark Thompson, TV astronomer and author, uses some fun demonstrations along the way to help illustrate the challenges facing human spaceflight, from early attempts at rocket propulsion through to the use of toilets and even overcoming the challenges of sex in zero gravity!

Description: Les Inouis speaks about humanity without words! Five artists from different backgrounds tell the tragic story of a migrant's deafening silence. They tell about his dreams of freedom, washed up on the shores of a free country. Just as the wolf in a fairytale, the Other is a reality one can't put aside in the context of a complex and manipulated world. In his new creation, between documentary and fantasy, between reality and virtual world, Patrick Masset sheds light on the relation between the image (video), our connected world and an ancestral art called theatre.

Title: Abouttimeyousaurus: Meet The Newest Dinosaurs
Teaser: Join Dr Stephen Brusatte as he introduces some of the most amazing new dinosaur discoveries and talk about his adventures digging up dinosaurs across the globe.
Description: We are currently in the middle of a golden age of dinosaur discovery, with palaeontologists finding a new species of dinosaur somewhere around the world on average once a week! Just last year about 50 new species were found, ranging from one of the biggest long-necked dinosaurs ever discovered, to a four-winged dinosaur that could fly, to a weird long-snouted tyrannosaur, discovered in China by a team including Dr Stephen Brusatte from The University of Edinburgh. Join him as he introduces some of the most amazing new dinosaur discoveries and talk about his adventures digging up dinosaurs across the globe.

Title: Tiernan Douieb: The World's Full of Idiots, Let's Live in Space
Description: Commander Chris Hadfield said that six months on the International Space Station made him feel a great sense of just how much the world is all one place and we are all one people living together on it. ‘Very friendly but fiercely political’ (Time Out) comedian Tiernan Douieb wonders why we have to send people quite so far away to have that realisation, and just how feasible is it to fire a large portion of the population into space until they behave?

Quantum Theatre’s stylish and whimsical production presents a magical flight of fancy where willow-the-wisp fairies, unsuspecting artisans and ardent young lovers are woven together by the finest gossamer thread.

What happens when you pry the real people from between the pages of history? What happens when the story of these women is finally told?

Title: Franks and Skinner Present: Myself and Myself
Description: Franks and Skinner dance, sing and improvise in their latest comic adventure. With over 20 characters, fast-paced comedy and classic 90s tunes, this show will tickle you in more ways than one (subject to guarantee). Myself and Myself is a surreal take on friendship, fertilisation and funkiness. Franks and Skinner create odd, dark humour from everyday events, and pick up on the quirks and idiosyncrasies of human nature. There are wigs, sequin jackets, a saxophone and the odd bike helmet! They're loud, they're proud, they're placid, they're flaccid. 'Very funny indeed' (FemaleArts.com).

Description: Scarlett Lane is about a dangerous journey down the red carpet. It tells the story of Tina Marshall's overnight rise to fame as she enters a place where singers forget how to sing, dancers forget why they’re dancing, and the girl in the mirror becomes a distant image. Why do so many accomplished singers rarely sing live, and what would the classic story of Jekyll and Hyde look like set in a world of paparazzi and public humiliation?

This is a jazz orchestra line up of saxophones, trumpets, trombones and a four-piece rhythm section bringing you swing, jazz and Latin tunes through the eras. You may recognise tunes from Duke Ellington, Count Basie and Glenn Miller and our guest vocalists bring you numbers made famous by the likes of Frank Sinatra, Tony Bennett and Michael Bublé. Title: Stop Brushing Your Teeth!
Description: The common phrase 'an apple a day, keeps the doctor away' sounds quite sensible in promoting healthy living, doesn’t it? However, a quick internet search suggests that eating an apple a day will: keep the doctor away if you’re a woman, over 50; not keep the doctor away; send you running to the dentist. So we’re surrounded by a lot of contradictory and confusing information. Join Professor Jan Clarkson, one of the world’s leading experts on oral health, as she discusses what we actually know about looking after your teeth and what’s nothing more than pseudoscience.
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.
Artist: Cabaret of Dangerous Ideas / Fair Pley

The giant 150 capacity yurt, an original tented structure from Eastern Europe, will surprise and delight! Food, drink and The Famous Spiegeltent on site too.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Monsters, Pirates and Silly Songs
Description: Charlotte and Adam Guillain perform Pizza for Pirates, their latest hilarious story in the George's Amazing Adventures series. There will be very strange monsters, plenty of puppets, some silly songs and lots of pirate jokes as you join George on his search for a real pirate crew. Tickets admit 1 child and 1 accompanying adult. Adult supervision recommended.

Title: Abdel Bari Atwan
Subtitle: How Islamic State Conquered Cyberspace
Description: A familiar face in the British media, Abdel Bari Atwan interviewed Osama Bin Laden and is a leading voice in interpreting Islamist militancy for western audiences. For his new book Islamic State: The Digital Caliphate, Atwan interviewed insiders from the global jihadi movement, and seeks to explain the strategy behind IS’s acts of ruthless, horrific violence. Today he explains the group's ideological differences with Al-Qaeda and its masterful command of social media.

Title: Jay Kadn (formerly Junai Kaden)
Description:
Jay Kadn, the artist formerly known as Junai Kaden is back once again, and better than ever! Kadn is an British Pakistani singer/songwriter & multi instrumentalist from Essex, London. He has had a huge amount of success in the past with number one signles on the iTunes Worldwide Chart & The Official BBC Asian Download Chart. Under his new name, Jay Kadn is now a independent/unsigned act which everyone has their eye on for 2015 and beyond. There is no doubt Kadn is one artist to watch out for… especially at this year’s Edinburgh Mela!

Part of a full day programme of events - ticket prices are per day. Free entry for children under 12. Timings subject to change.
Venue address:
Leith Links
Opposite Duncan Place
Edinburgh
Venue accessibility:
The site is fully accessible, although it must be noted that the festival is an outdoor event on a largely grass surface. Accessible toilets will be provided and assistance will be available for disabled patrons at the box office and the site entrance.
A very limited number of parking spaces will be available for disabled visitors in the production carpark just off John's Place

Title: Gay Furnish Flirt Coach
Description: Character comedian Charlotte McDougall (Bearded Ladies, Radio 4) is Gay Furnish, sexologist and dating guru. Gay's masterclass introduces a squad of guest gurus and mentors. 'Do you have zero charisma? Are you sweaty and awkward but yearn for intimacy? Are you an introvert, an extrovert or a pervert? Don't criticise yourself, spend time with yourself, play with yourself. I can change your life. No, seriously. I can.' 'Impressive stuff. Comedy with its head on, with flashes of sheer genius' **** (Scotsman). 'Mad. Absolutely bonkers. But very funny' **** (Daily Express). 'Unmissable' ***** (Daily Mail).
Venue description: Now in its 16th year, Underbelly Cowgate is home to some of the best talent and the best bars you can find at the Fringe. Complete with a Cow Cafe (serving up coffee, snacks and free late-night entertainment), three licensed bars and seven vivacious venues open til 5am.

Title: Akiko Okamoto Piano Recital
Description: This talented, Japanese-born pianist returns to Edinburgh to perform two delightful programmes of piano works from Bach to Bartok, Mozart to Prokofiev, and including Beethoven, Chopin, Schubert, Brahms and Liszt.
Venue: St Andrew's and St George's West, George St
Venue description: A beautiful, easily accessible 18th century New Town church, which hosts a variety of musical performances - from soloists to choirs, instrumentalists to small orchestras and bands in all musical genres: classical, folk, jazz, songs from the shows, opera, world music.  Enjoy light lunches and snacks in the Undercroft cafe, or sit and admire the newly refurbished building.

Title: Science Brings Us Together
Teaser: This informative, invigorating and inspiring panel discussion will examine ways in which diplomatic science can build bridges between disparate communities, help resolve conflict and foster international collaboration and development.
Description: While there is much in the world that can divide people, science is a common language that can unify them. This informative, invigorating and inspiring panel discussion will examine ways in which diplomatic science can build bridges between disparate communities, help resolve conflict and foster international collaboration and development. Featuring journalist Priya Shetty, who specialises in health and humanitarian issues in developing countries and Prof Yasser Khalil from SESAME, a synchrotron facility in Jordan that encourages a culture of peace through international cooperation in science. Chaired by Ewan Aitken of the Cyrenians.

Title: Dazzle Jewellery Exhibition and Nuno Scarves
Description: Since 1983 Dazzle has been showing up to 50 leading contemporary jewellery designers from all over the world. 3,000 pieces. This year we are adding a new dimension – the much sought after world-famous Japanese handmade scarves by Nuno Textiles. Nearby Cafe Stag is a wonderful coffee shop with the most delicious home-made soups and hand-made cakes. A reason in itself for visiting the beautiful Dovecot Studios. This is a selling exhibition. Exhibitors include Jane Adam, Sophie Harley, Zsuzsi Morrison, Naoko Yoshizawa, stylish watchmaker Justin Duance, Lesley Strickland and Dot Sim. Admission free.
Venue description: Dovecot Studios is a one hundred year old tapestry studio, now homed in a beautifully renovated Victorian swimming pool in the heart of Edinburgh. As well as housing the tapestry studio, we also have exhibitions, venue hire, cafe and our shop.

Title: Greg Shapiro's Pick of the Fringe
Description: Gregory Shapiro (Comedy Central, Boom Chicago) celebrates 25 years in comedy by hosting a showcase for some of his favorite acts on the Fringe. He’s organised tours with Brendon Burns, Glenn Wool, Desiree Burch, etc. And as co-host of The Amsterdam Comedy Podcast, Shapiro offers some of his favourite new talent from the Continent. Pay attention. There will be a quiz. Winners receive free Scotch whisky, sponsored by Shapiro's app The Quickest Quiz.
Venue description: Fringe Venue 462

Title: Walking the Tightrope: The Tension Between Art and Politics
Description: World premiere of explosive political short plays by writers including Caryl Churchill, Neil LaBute and Timberlake Wertenbaker, followed by energetic post-show audience discussions with stellar panels exploring freedom of expression in the UK arts today. 'Superb ... An incredibly important production' ***** (TheMetropolist.com). 'Bravo! ... Truly entertains while challenging, and that is no mean feat!' (HuffingtonPost.co.uk).
Warnings: Contains strong language and scenes of a graphic nature
Artist: Offstage and Underbelly Productions, in association with Theatre Uncut
Venue description: Potterrow is the location of Topside, a stunning studio theatre presenting the very best in Fringe theatre, comedy and cabaret.

Title: Sandbach School Big Band
Description: This acclaimed big band return to the Fringe for the third time, having previously sold out. They recreate the magnificent sounds of the Motown era in the spectacular surrounding of the Great Hall.
Venue description: The Royal College of Physicians, Edinburgh (RCPE) is a spectacular Georgian venue providing four unique spaces for JLJ Creative's shows and exhibitions. Large scale music is in the stunning Victorian great hall, chamber music and poetry lies in the original library. The Queen Mother conference centre hosts drama in the lecture theatre and three exhibitions in its foyer.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Lift level access to all areas, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Stairs outside the venue

Title: The Internet is Not the Answer
Teaser: The worldwide web is now a quarter of a century old but has it fostered a new renaissance or is it encouraging a culture of distraction, vulgarity and narcissism?
Description: The worldwide web is now a quarter of a century old and there can be no doubt it has transformed the world. But according to entrepreneur, writer and Techcrunch host Andrew Keen, this disruption has also been a terrible failure. Is the unregulated digital world making us poorer rather than wealthier? Causing unemployment rather than generating jobs? Empowering mob rule rather than promoting democracy? And, rather than fostering a new renaissance, it is encouraging a culture of distraction, vulgarity and narcissism? Join Andrew in conversation with John Naughton technology columnist of The Observer and Vice President of Wolfson College, Cambridge.

Title: Hellions
Description: Multi-award winning director Bruce McDonald returns to EIFF with this horrifying tale of mayhem, madness, murderous evil munchkins and a young girl home alone at night. Unaware that her pregnant condition has piqued the interest of the evil pumpkin field spirits, teenager Dora needs some time alone to think. Very soon the evil trick-or-treaters arrive to claim their prize, and Dora finds herself fighting for her life. Beautifully shot in an unearthly magenta glow, and set against a creepy, atmospheric score, this is Halloween horror at its best.

Title: App Developer Workshop
Teaser: Learn how to become an app developer and create and use your very own smartphone app.
Description: Learn how to become an app developer and create and use your very own smartphone app. You'll learn the essentials of designing and programming a mobile app for iPhone or Android, using an intuitive and easy to use platform that's perfect for first-timers but also loaded with features for more adventurous developers.

Title: Routines
Description: Life as a stand-up comedian is all about the routines. And not all of them happen on stage. A brand new and immersive fusion of stand-up comedy and theatre that allows you to see the full picture. It's stand-up. From both sides of the curtain. Starring Dana Alexander (BBC's Russell Howard's Good News), Stephen Carlin (Comedy Central's Alternative Comedy Experience), Will Mars (BBC's Stand-Up for Comic Relief) and Matt Roper (BBC Radio 4 Extra's The Comedy Club). Produced by Will Mars (Creator of award-winning show and BBC2 pilot, Joke Thieves). Directed by Michael Eriera (Scotsman Fringe First Award Winner).
Venue description: Edinburgh's premiere party venue and the free mega venue with six rooms of free shows running throughout the day and night, all located around a vibrant and buzzing courtyard. With a huge drinks selection, a wide menu, hog roast, and plenty of new surprises each year! Shows run from 09:00-02:00, with music and dancing trough until 5am, the venue is barely ever closed in August.

Title: Al Porter Is Yours
Description: Al Porter Is Yours is the irreverent debut show from Ireland's newest comedy star. At 22, Al falls in love daily, has 'completed' Tinder and is still a mammy's boy! A parish secretary's son, Al was supposed to be a priest – until he slept with one and changed his mind. A socialite on a social welfare budget, Al has been on countless dates, gotten into debt and was sued by a presidential candidate! In this candid hour he pours over the details of it all in his playful style that's been described as council-estate camp.
Warnings: The show contains some mild to strong language.
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces and seven bars including the exclusive roof top bar, The Loft. A must for all Fringe-goers. A massive mini-Fringe under one roof, this iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe! All spaces, the café and all seven bars are wheelchair accessible, with the exception of the Balcony and Billiard Rooms. Tickets available 24-hours online!

Title: Return of the Snot Zombies
Description: The Snot Zombies are back! More bogies, books and bottom burps with award-winning author Stuart Reid and his crazy characters, Gorgeous George and Grandpa Jock. Definitely see this before lunch.

Title: The Arup Lecture 2015: Old Cities, New Ways, Perpetual Places
Teaser: How can new materials and new manufacturing, installing and monitoring techniques in design, engineering and construction preserve and enhance a great city like Edinburgh?
Description: How can new materials and new manufacturing, installing and monitoring techniques in design, engineering and construction preserve and enhance a great city like Edinburgh? Graham Dodd and Graham Gedge of the Material Consulting Group within Arup will share a possible cutting-edge future for our city, where important heritage buildings will be preserved and their performance enhanced, and new buildings and infrastructure will be more responsive to their surroundings and make less environmental impact.

Title: Elsie Diamond: The Sensible Dresser
Description: Elsie Diamond international burlesque bombshell and singer presents this one-woman show, inspired by her day job: dresser to the stars in the unpredictable world of costume. A comic, sexy and heartfelt piece told through comic song and striptease. With her vintage looks, a voice from a bygone era and exquisite costumes, Elsie transports you effortlessly through different eras whilst maintaining her very modern sense of humour. Having worked in television, opera and theatre, Elsie tells tales from her own and friends' costume careers. With some artistic license… These stories can’t possibly be true, can they?
Venue description: CC Blooms has been part of the furniture of Edinburgh nights out for as long as most of us can remember. Born in the early 90s as a wonderfully cheesy gay club, the venue recently reopened following extensive refurbishment. www.ccbloomsedinburgh.com

Title: Michael J Dolan: Miserable Guts
Description: Comedy's bleak philosopher is back asking the questions nobody else will. When did I last go outside? Am I already dead? How are you meant to maintain a happy marriage in the face of the unstoppable decay of everything that exists? Stand-up comedy for people who are too tired to get angry. 'Skilful humour from the very dark side' **** (Sunday Times). 'Inherently funny' **** (Chortle.co.uk). 'A very, very funny man' **** (Skinny).
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.
Venue description: Across the road from the original venue Stand 1, Stand 3 is a superb large theatre space with its own bar, and Stand 4 an intimate studio with exciting Fringe debuts. Venues accessible through courtyard at basement level.

Title: TES
Description: Tess of the D'Urbervilles re-imagined. Contemporary theatrical adaptation of Thomas Hardy's celebrated novel in which the tragic heroine is reinvented for the 21st century as a teenage boy from a Newcastle council estate, who is found to be descended from a famous Romantic poet. Spoken word theatre from poet, musician, and Hammer & Tongue poetry slam founder Steve Larkin. 'An Orwellian portrayal of Britain's rotting underbelly that slices like a rusty razor' ***** (Victoria Times). 'Remarkable storytelling' **** (Canadian Broadcasting Corporation). 'Prepare to leave stunned and inspired by the power of Larkin's spoken word' ***** (Edmonton Sun). www.stevelarkin.com
Warnings: Graphic sexual description.
Venue description: Come and graze in George Square! Food, drink, two fantastic venues and of course, an upside down purple cow. If you're looking for Udderbelly or Wee Coo, this is the place to be. We also have buzzing bars open til very late!

Title: Come Together, Barb Jungr and John McDaniel Perform The Beatles
Description: In this exciting collaboration, award-winning vocalist and performer, Jungr, and Grammy and Emmy Award winner McDaniel investigate The Beatles; celebrating Paul, John, George and Ringo with new, often unexpected arrangements. John, arranger and music director of some great stars of American theatre and cabaret, was arranger and music director for eight Broadway musicals. Jungr reinvented European and British cabaret, with extensive, acclaimed explorations of Dylan, Cohen and more. With their mutual love of these great songs, John's superb arrangements, and Jungr's performance; this promises to be very special indeed.
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.
Venue description: The iconic Assembly Rooms building is at the heart of Edinburgh's New Town, bringing the best of the Fringe to the city centre. Following an extensive restoration programme and hugely successful re-opening 2012, this stunning venue offers opulent surroundings with the highest standards throughout. The 2015 Assembly Rooms Fringe presents the very best in theatre, comedy, music and entertainment.

Title: Cathedral Chamber Music – Mezzo-Soprano, Viola, Piano
Description: Three of Scotland's most exciting young professional musicians unite to perform ravishing repertoire for voice, viola and piano, including Brahms, Poulenc, Rubbra, Falla and Loeffler. Full details at www.cathedral.net.

Title: Coughing Sheep
Description: Desperately hunting last minute leading man, Lucy Frederick reluctantly presents her father, keen rambler and tropical fish enthusiast Peter Henderson in the lost Russian classic Coughing Sheep. Can dad-dancing cut the vatrushka? This is Lucy Frederick's third Edinburgh; Pursuit of Cool 2013, Claw of Anxiety 2014. ‘Strong, wonderfully light-hearted,  enjoyable’. Four stars (ThreeWeeks). 'Delightful' (BroadwayBaby.com). ‘Great comic timing!' (Stage). Peter Henderson returns following his hit one-man show, Who Did I Think I Was? 2014. ‘Terrific, beautifully observed performance, laugh out loud funny', four stars, (Scotsman). Five stars (BroadwayBaby.com). Five stars (EdFringeReview.com). Four stars (Edinburgh.FringeGuru.com). Four stars (Fringereview.com).

Title: Alex Smith - The Art of Grooming
Description: Have you ever felt that perhaps you have too much money? That the money you have set aside for a house, a car or that kidney transplant a doctor has told you that you critically need, could be put to better use? Perhaps it could be better spent making someone else's hand worth more than most people's car? Well then perhaps you, like Alex, have recently decided to get engaged. Stand-up, Huffington Post columnist and You and Your Wedding magazine's resident groom Alex Smith takes you on his wedding journey.
Venue description: With live music every night, ranging from acoustic to punk to tribute acts, the cavernous ‘Binkies is often crammed with loyal gig goers having a grand old time. 18+ age restriction. www.whistlebinkies.com

Title: The Fiery Path
Description: Should one mistake condemn a man to hell? Blues legend Robert Johnson's choice is explored whilst taking the fiery path. Three Nottinghamshire A-Level students bring you their own devised dramatic creation in Revolutionary Theatre's Fringe debut! The actors sing and play live music, and require (some) audience participation; the circumstances of famous people's own fiery paths become personal to the audience in this way. Please come along to enjoy the product of our imagination; we aim to leave an intangible mark upon your mind! Revolutionary Theatre is a team of visionaries!
Venue description: Spotlites is one of the leading venues at Edfringe, with three unique, beautiful theatres established at the heart of the Festival. Our central, easy to find venue, 40m from Princes Street, presents an outstanding programme of international companies, interactive children's theatre, drama workshops, innovative plays, musicals, dance, music, magic, poetry, comedy and cabaret. Spotlites has a repuation for quality five and four star sell-outs, clean facilities and caring, helpful staff.
Venue accessibility: Some of our shows are Captioned and BSL Signed. We also offer relaxed performances. Please ask for our water bowl if you have a thirsty guide dog! Further information about individual theatres and shows is available from the Box Office or by phone on 01634 829468 or by email on office@spotlites.co.uk or visit http://spotlites.co.uk/sate-xaccess.shtml. Title: Northerners – Rory Lewis Photographic Exhibition
Description: Rory Lewis Photographer has made an outstanding contribution to photography and the visual arts, creating consistently imaginative and thought-provoking portraits. Rory’s Northerners exhibition is an entirely new collection of portraits from a cross section of Northern celebrities, sports personalities, actors, politicians and people encountered. Featuring sittings with Sir Ian McKellen, Sir Patrick Stewart, Ian McShane, Emma Rigby, Claire Sweeney and many others.

Title: Johnny Danger DIY Spy: Licenced to Thrill
Description: School boy Jonathan Dangerfield has always dreamed of being a spy and it seems his fake online spy profile has worked when MI6 are fooled into recruiting him. Will he get found out whilst trying to stay one step ahead of the baddies? Join New Zealand author Peter Millett with his hilarious new action-packed spy series Johnny Danger, DIY Spy.

Title: Plain English
Description: Terry Burns writes and performs and Clara Onyemere directs this comedic one-man play, with a dramatic twist, that charts the trials and tribulations of an idealistic newly qualified English teacher as he starts work in an inner city London comprehensive school. The play follows the protagonist as he deals with an array of colourful characters from the old school Head of Department Mr Cooper, with his steadfast belief in discipline and his penchant for pickled eggs to the belligerent and cocksure Wayne who is determined to achieve his dreams. It'll make you laugh and cry! Come see it!
Venue description: theSpaceUK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Poetry Can F*ck Off
Description: By Heathcote Williams (Herald Lifetime Achievement Award winner). Poetry f*cks off tyrants. The right words can get under the skin of those in power and spark revolution. Featuring the lyrics and verse of Jim Morrison, Billie Holiday, Sophie Scholl, Martin Luther King, William Blake, Arundhati Roy, Victor Jara, Gil Scott-Heron, Lupe Fiasco and many others, this is a celebration of those who have spoken out against tyranny while making our hearts pound. Performed by Roy Hutchins, Sameena Zehra, Selina Nwulu, Jonny Fluffypunk and special guests, with live music from Dr Blue. ‘Mind-swaying’ (Michael McClure).
Warnings: Some strong language – adult themes.
Venue description: Summerhall presents engaging, challenging, high-quality theatre, dance, literature, visual art and music for people of all ages.  Our unique home in the former Dick Vet building of the University of Edinburgh offers atmospheric performance spaces, a buzzy courtyard and an onsite pub, the Royal Dick Bar, with something for everyone to explore, discover and enjoy - “an entire festival in its own right” The Guardian
Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café.
We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please do not hesitate to contact us by phone on 0845 874 3000 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

http://www.summerhall.co.uk/about/accessibility/. Title: Big Bang Bash
Teaser: Join us for an out-of-this-world party celebrating the wonders of space.
Description: An out-of-this-world party celebrating the wonders of space. Sample a space-themed cocktail from the Bar at the End of the Universe, discover the solar system in our portable planetarium then have a go at making your own space craft to take home. Challenge yourself to build an interstellar structure using Splatform, watch roving scientists perform mind-boggling experiments, hear short talks from space experts, including authours Marcus Chown, Prof Monica Grady and Dr Roberto Trotta, or relax and enjoy vintage sci-films and our space-tacular DJ.

Title: Joel Creasey: The Hurricane
Description: Joel is Australia’s hottest comedy star right now. Fresh from sold out shows and critical acclaim in Melbourne, New York, London, Montreal and Sydney. He’s garnered critical acclaim and five-star reviews around the world while leaving a trail of comedic annihilation in his wake. Joel hits Edinburgh with his hot new show, join him for a night of laughs delivered in signature Creasey style – strap in, bitches... a hurricane is coming. Directed by Janelle Koenig. 'Master raconteur' (Advocate.com). ‘An inevitable star' ***** (Time Out, New York). ‘A young genius and a ruthless wit’ (Age, Melbourne).

Title: Gill Arbuthnott on My Family and Other Animals and Prospero's Cell
Subtitle: Reading Workshop
Description: Author and biologist Gill Arbuthnott looks at My Family and Other Animals by Gerald Durrell and Prospero's Cell by his brother Lawrence Durrell. Gerald's book is an autobiographical account of his childhood on Corfu which details his family and all the island’s fauna, whilst Lawrence provides a guide to the landscape and manners of the island. Expect an open discussion from the start: you can either read the books ahead of the event or be inspired to pick them up afterwards.

Title: Torna a Sorrento – Dinner and Show
Description: Let Philip Contini take you back to Sorrento for songs, stories, sunshine, romance, Neapolitan food and wine. With his Be Happy Band live on stage. Savour a three course Neapolitan dinner, pre-performance. Every year a sell-out show! 'Charming renditions of well-known Italian numbers. It’s a delightful event that sells out every year and it’s not hard to see why’ **** (BroadwayBaby.com).
Warnings: Dinner with background music. Performance after dinner.
Artist: Philip Contini and his Be Happy Band
Venue description: Music and cabaret stage space within the first floor restaurant in VinCaffe. An established Italian restaurant, cafe and wine bar on two floors in Edinburgh's newest city centre street in the heart of retail shopping in Edinburgh.

Title: Morgan Berry: Watership Down
Description: Join award-winning character comedian Joe Rowntree for the rare and wonderful specimen Morgan Berry: Pet Bereavement Counsellor. Rabbit Specialist. Born in Barnsley, raised in Africa – Bafrican! The car wash is in trouble. Morgan must save it. Can his online course in Pet Bereavement yield dividends and stop it from going Watership Down. ‘It is his use of very specific and nonsensical language that is so captivatingly funny’ **** (Chortle.co.uk). ‘Short of breath and with tear drenched cheeks, we watched the show end as unexpectedly as it began’ **** (InformedEdinburgh.co.uk).
Venue description: The Banshee Labyrinth is a teeming pub that is said to be Scotland's most haunted pub. Regular comedy nights, karaoke and live music will keep you entertained until the wee small hours. Three performance spaces, three bars, one open from 12.30-05:00. 18+ only. www.thebansheelabyrinth.com

Title: Pistol Pete Wearn - Footstomping Acoustic Blues
Description: Tearing it up with his own raucous interpretation of traditional blues, Pistol Pete Wearn is a renowned vocalist, slide guitarist, harmonica player and songwriter. Equipped with acoustic guitar and stompbox he blends traditional material and originals with the odd slide-ifed cover.

Artist: Pistol Pete Wearn / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Holding

Title: Rory MacLean
Subtitle: The Quest for New Soviet Man
Description: When the USSR dissolved in 1991, a narrow sliver of land next to the Ukraine declared independence. Transnistria now has its own Leninist government, but is still not recognised by any other country in the world. Photojournalist Nick Danziger and author Rory MacLean spent time with Bentley-driving, AK47-wielding oligarchs in Gucci tracksuits to create an absorbing illustrated study of a region whose fate will affect the whole of Europe. Chaired by Jamie Jauncey.

Title: Howard Jacobson
Subtitle: The Booker Man Gets Reflective
Description: A welcome return to Charlotte Square Gardens for the winner of the Man Booker Prize in 2010 who was also shortlisted last year for his acclaimed Huxley-esque dystopian drama, J. Recently, Howard Jacobson has been reflecting in the media on one of his early novels which is now out of print. Meet an author whose recent prize successes represent the literary acclaim he has long deserved.

Title: Ruby Zajac
Description: 'Her voice has a sultry, husky undertone, and her lyrics are filled with witty metaphors which make her songs both playful yet touching at the same time' (CamCreatives.co.uk). Raised in Scotland's vibrant folk milieu, Ruby Zajac is an emerging songwriter with thoughtful, memorable songs. Accompanying herself on guitar, and with sister Iona providing beautiful vocal harmonies, Ruby's AMC Fringe debut might just make you think a little differently as you walk out of the Back Room, humming one of her tunes. ‘Climb that rock / You could be that eagle, soaring through the treetops.’

'Anyone who likes MJ Hibbett will have a much nicer life' (Robin Ince). 'Amazing! Like two drunken dads picking up a guitar at a party!' (Radio 1). 'MJ Hibbett – Top of the Pops!' (Eddie Argos).
Artist: MJ Hibbett (and Steve) / PBH’s Free Fringe
Venue description: Sneaky Pete's is a one room club located on the Cowgate. The programming at the club is student-friendly, with guest DJs playing throughout the week as well as at weekends. As well as operating as a club, Sneaky Pete's has a full schedule of early evening live music performances. 18+ only www.sneakypetes.co.uk/

Title: The Temptation of St Anthony
Description: Inspired by the ancient legend of a man who spent 35 years in solitude in the Egyptian desert, this Wellcome Trust-supported ensemble performance explores, through song and body, landscapes where mental health and religious experience collide. How to treat a religiously-orientated mental illness? This is a problem facing NHS psychiatrists treating patients who say they are possessed by spirits. Is there a limit to what Western medicine can heal, when faced with a dark night of the soul? With insight from psychiatry and anthropology, this show plunges soul-first into the human experience of demon possession.
Venue description: Summerhall presents engaging, challenging, high-quality theatre, dance, literature, visual art and music for people of all ages.  Our unique home in the former Dick Vet building of the University of Edinburgh offers atmospheric performance spaces, a buzzy courtyard and an onsite pub, the Royal Dick Bar, with something for everyone to explore, discover and enjoy - “an entire festival in its own right” The Guardian

FlashMob begins as a game of words and ends as a dance party for all participants – with audience members interacting with movement artists and controlling lights and sounds. At its heart, FlashMob is about the simple joy of play, enhanced by cutting-edge technology. It is our pleasure to present you with a place where your actions and choices are an integral part of the performance – a unique theatrical experience, unlike anything you have seen before. Stand up, jump in, and enjoy the show!

You'll learn how computer programming works using a fun card game and code your own game using Scratch. You'll try some interactive electronics and use supercool Makey-Makeys to make a piano out of bananas. There will also be the chance to design and make your own games controller and build a brushbot robotic bug.

Description: There are no rules in Churchill’s experimental play on the preoccupations of modern living. The key is to sit back and allow this visceral experience to take its cumulative effect. This highly charged blend of tragedy and comedy invites the audience to consider the saturation of information that modern day connectivity has provided us with. Performed by a versatile company of young players, Love and Information plays on 21st century audiences' capacity to absorb, decipher and derive meaning in an instant – whilst simultaneously questioning the effect of this ability on our lives.

An intergenerational tale of what we live for and what we leave behind. Gary McNair returns to the Traverse after last year’s award-winning five-star show Donald Robertson is Not a Stand-Up Comedian: ‘A tour de force and a must-see’ ***** (Stage). ‘Brilliantly conceived’ **** (Scotsman). **** (Guardian). **** (Times)'. www.madeinscotlandshowcase.com

'Remarkably accomplished stage presence ... blistering material which pushes dangerously near the boundaries of good taste' (Sunday Times). Sailor lives for robbery, imprisonment and expulsion. Be his victim. Sailor's virtues are simple: rent, theft, and betrayal. Join him. ‘Great drama has the power to inform, move and make shifts in consciousness. Thief has all this.’ ***** (Sarah Agnew, Brighton Argus). ‘Sensational. Ferocious. Acted with great intensity. A memorable hour of theatre.’ (Joyce McMillan, Scotsman). ‘Tantalisingly layered, cloaked in the dreamy mingling of pain, sex and desire.’ (BroadwayBaby.com).

David Kinloch, professor of poetry and creative writing at the University of Strathclyde, plays his role in rectifying this with a glorious new short collection of poems, Some Women. Feisty, irreverent and at times downright outraged, Kinloch’s women speak their minds in vivid, memorable voices.

Title: Sensory Experimentation
Teaser: Join us for an experimental exploration of the surprising links between our senses and our taste buds.
Description: Join us for an experimental exploration of the surprising links between our senses and our taste buds. With the head of the University of Oxford's Crossmodal Research Laboratory Prof Charles Spence, scent technician Ericka Duffy and former Head of Culinary Research and Development at the Nordic Food lab, Ben Reade. Through a series of experiments and tricksome tasters we will delve in to sensuous flavours, smells and textures to intrigue and excite your palette. Dinner will never be the same again!

Title: Unexpected Items in Badinage Areas
