Title: Sally Gardner & David Levithan
Description: Join two of the best authors writing for young people today. From the US, David Levithan joins us to discuss his new novel Another Day, the follow-up to the acclaimed Every Day. Sally Gardner's latest book The Door That Led to Where features three friends on a journey to unravel mysteries of the past. Join them to hear about brilliant stories that give a voice to young people.

Title: The Bollywood Express
Description: Bollywood... rich, flamboyant, loud and downright entertaining! Presented to you by the students of The Aditya Birla Integrated School, India, a school for children with learning difficulties. The Bollywood Express will halt at the Fringe for the first time ever to lead you on a journey that is a perfect blend of spicy Desi drama, emotion and of course, dance! Watch them become India's next big super hit! All aboard The Bollywood Express!
Venue description: What better way to be celebrating turning 10 years old in 2015 than with a brand new venue? Three really is the magic number so say hello to the newest addition to the family and our third venue - Greenside @ Infirmary Street!

Title: Meet Me in Montenegro
Description: Writer/director Alex Holdridge’s indie film, the award-winning In Search of a Midnight Kiss, embraced a heady romance between two people on New Year’s Eve in Los Angeles. This time round, he and co-writer/director Linnea Saasen head over to Europe for the story of Anderson (Holdridge). On a trip to Berlin, he bumps into old flame Lina (Saasen), a Norwegian dancer he met in Montenegro some years earlier. This brings back memories of their brief but intense romance..

Title: Touch
Description: Jacky used to teach people how to see and understand each other better. But when she starts to find that difficult in her own life, it unleashes a dark habit from within her. Despite her lifetime of training Jacky no longer wants you to see and understand her as well as you wish. But that's the reason you came! Touch is a warm and charming story that guides you through the calamitous forgotten corners of our sense of self-worth. 'Come sit next to a stranger, maybe you'll fall in love. It's happened before!'
Warnings: Contains strong language. Deals with themes of self-harm and mild sexuality.
Artist: Ciarán Myers in Association with Asylon Theatre / Universal Arts
Venue description: Home to quality, professional, UK and international performing arts. It is situated in the beautifully and lavishly decorated Freemasons Hall built in 1913, on the elegant George Street, between Assembly Rooms and International Book Festival. Most beautiful Fringe venue with well-equipped and comfortable theatres. Winner of Best Fringe Venue, Edinburgh Spotlight. 'A top-notch theatre programme' ([i]Stage[/i]).

Title: Avicide
Description: Roger is a man trapped in his Waterloo flat because he believes all the birds have left London's Southbank to spite him and they may attack at any moment. Avicide deals with how easy it is to get lost in the system and forgotten by the people you need most. Warnings: Contains swearing and moderate sexual reference.

Title: Billy Through the Window
Description: ‘It’s a secret, Billy. That means we can’t say anything, and we can’t be seen.’ At a children’s care home, Joe and Billy meet. The boys do everything together. They brush their teeth to the same rhythm and fold their socks along identical lines. But when Billy gets ill, Joe can’t bear to be different. He takes Billy to a hideout and sets two rules: no more medicine, nobody needs to know. A thrilling and tender new play from Bristol Old Vic writer-in-attachment Tabitha Mortiboy and the critically acclaimed Bellow Theatre. 'Brimming with new talent' (Guide2Bristol.com).

Subtitle: The Essence of Tolstoy; The Soul of Pamuk
Description: Nowhere are the decisions of the translator more forensically picked over than in a translation of one of the classics. Fortunately, Rosamund Bartlett’s new version of Tolstoy’s Anna Karenina is the most accomplished of several recent translations. Meanwhile Maureen Freely is best known for her translation of five novels by leading Turkish author, Orhan Pamuk. Both are exceptional translators and today they discuss their craft. Chaired by James Runcie.

Title: Claire Ford: Box
Description: Outside a cardboard box? Then how do you think inside it? This and other conundrums solved with heartfelt storytelling, clowning, and double walled chipboard. Box clever comedy for the unboxed. Title: Follow the Heart
Description: Follow the Heart is a modern dance drama presented by six public amateur dancers from Shanghai Himalayas Museum [M Theatre]. Title: Extreme
Teaser: From Icarus to Evel Knievel, humanity has always been fascinated by those who live on the edge. But are some of us wired to seek danger and risk?
Description: From Icarus to Evel Knievel, humanity has always been fascinated by those who live on the edge. But are some of us wired to seek danger and risk? Join behavioural scientist Dr Paul Martin, psychologist and author Emma Barrett and world explorer Tim Jarvis for tales of cave-dwelling scientists, polar perils, starvation, solitude and resilience as we examine the astonishing limits of human endurance.

Title: Hey, I'm Alive!
Description: A durational performance from the critically acclaimed, award-winning Creative Electric. Cystic fibrosis sufferers are discouraged from meeting one another as it increases the risk of infection. Imagine never physically connecting with someone who understands what your future holds because they’re heading in the same direction. Hey, I’m Alive! is a highly visual, durational performance by five performers, one of whom has CF. Each performer is placed inside their own Zorb with a thin layer of latex protecting them from infection. Audiences are free to wander amongst them, interact and observe them and listen to their stories.
Venue description: Dance Base is a National Centre for Dance housed in an award-winning and fully-accessible venue in the heart of the historic old town. Title: Austensibility
Description: Since 2002, the Mercators, one of Edinburgh's longest established amateur theatre groups, have presented costumed dramatised readings celebrating famous writers such as Charles Dickens, Oscar Wilde and Arthur Conan Doyle. This year we return to Jane Austen for the second time, documenting her life with her own words from her letters and reminiscences from family and acquaintances, illustrated with short extracts from her novels including Sense and Sensibility, Pride and Prejudice, Emma, and Persuasion. We also spotlight some of her lesser-known juvenilia, written by the teenage Jane for her own amusement and to entertain her family.

Title: The Taking of Pelham One Two Three
Description:
Having directed several notable American TV movies during the period in focus, including The Marcus Nelson Murders and the much loved The Night That Panicked America, the late Joseph Sargent (1925 - 2014) should have featured in this year’s “Little Big Screen” strand, but the availability and rights issues surrounding these titles proved insurmountable.
As it would be unthinkable not to acknowledge the acclaimed Sargent in that context, we are presenting instead this special retrospective screening of his most popular big screen outing.
Famously referenced by Tarantino in Reservoir Dogs, Sargent’s cult classic sees an armed gang hijack a New York subway train full of commuters, forcing a downbeat transit cop (Walter Matthau) into a battle of wits with their wily leader (Robert Shaw). Briefly turning his expert attention from television to cinema, Sargent delivered one of the definitive thrillers of the era, boasting powerhouse performances from Matthau and Shaw, and an unforgettably cool score by David Shire.

Title: Bruce Fummey: Scottish Comedian of the Year Winner 2014
Description: Multi award-winning Scottish Ghanaian stand-up tells stories old and new from life and wanderings. ‘Thank God – or Braveheart – for Bruce Fummey... This man exudes infectious warmth and humour’ (Chortle.co.uk) ‘Scotland's top stand-up’ (Daily Record). ‘…ingratiated with an easy affability ... but with mischievous twists’ (Scotsman). ‘You will be hard-pressed to find a more engaging performer on the Fringe than Bruce Fummey, do go and see this show’ (Chortle.co.uk). ‘…a joyous way to spend an hour’ (ThreeWeeks). ‘...put simply, he is a very, very funny man’ (Skinny, Edinburgh).

Code: Another World Is Possible: Traditional Stories, the Earth Charter and Fresh Thinking
Title: Another World Is Possible: Traditional Stories, the Earth Charter and Fresh Thinking
Description: The Earth Charter was developed after a worldwide dialogue on common goals and values for social justice, peace and sustainability. Over 300 traditional stories from around the world will be used as educational tools. These stories have been selected for their capacity to change our worldview, and our way of relating to our planet. Title: Padraig Potts’ Guide to Walking

Title: Sukshinder Shinda
Description:
Since his debut album, the instrumental album ‘Dhol Beat 1’ in 1989, Sukshinder Shinda has been garlanded with a number of honours around the world including ‘The UK Bhangra Music Awards – Best Producer,’ the PTC Punjabi Music Awards ‘Best Non Resident Punjabi Music Director’ for Collaborations 2, Best Video, Best Producer and Best Album at the UK AMAs, the BritAsia Music Awards Best Video for ‘Ghum Suhm,’ and last year a recognition of at the renowned 33rd All India Folk Art contest for the Indian Cultural Association in Kartarpur, Punjab.

Over his career, Shinda, who hails from the village of Dhamai, in the Hoshiarpur district of Punjab, has been the backbone for hit albums for artists such as Harbhajan Mann, Madan Maddi, Manjit Pappu, Nachhatar Gill, Amrinder Gill, AS Kang and for his formative and unique relationship with Jazzy B which still runs strong. Since he became a live act himself, he has extensively toured around the world as well as playing melas and festivals alongside the same acts he has produced music for. His live performances feel more like a concert as he wheels off some of his greatest hits and big Bhangra classics at will backed up by a band that has been with him from the beginning. His recent big video track ‘Dil Varda’ with Vancouver’s Harj Nagra furthered his position as a Punjabi singer of global appeal.

Description: The thought of being ‘locked in’ following a brain injury or aware during general anaesthesia troubles many of us. Title: The First Film
Description: Film-maker David Nicholas Wilkinson heads off on a mission to reveal the story of Louis Aimé Augustine Le Prince's pioneering work. In October 1888, Le Prince produced the world's first films in Leeds, England, shot on equipment patented in both America and the UK. Once he perfected his projection machine, he arranged to demonstrate his discovery in America. But on 16 September 1890, just weeks before he was due to sail to New York, he stepped onto the Dijon-Paris train and was never seen again. no body was ever found, so legally no one could fight the Le Prince claim to his invention.

In The Soul of the Marionette, Oxford professor of politics John Gray takes a quizzical look at the notion that we are really free at all. Gray draws on the literary work of Philip K Dick and Giacomo Leopardi, as well as philosophy and conspiracy theory logic, to show that we are increasingly remote from making real choices of our own.

Tony Webster has had a career, a single marriage and a calm divorce. He's certainly never tried to hurt anybody. Memory though is imperfect. Expect an open discussion from the start: you can either read the book ahead of the event or be inspired to pick it up afterwards.

Title: Confirmation

Of course, pinning me against a wall is exactly what I’d expect from someone like you.’ Confirmation is a show about the gulfs we can’t talk across, and about the way we choose to see only the evidence that proves we’re right. Working with research into the phenomenon of confirmation bias, Confirmation attempts to have an honourable dialogue, real and imagined, with political extremism. From multiple award-winning Chris Thorpe (Unlimited, Royal Exchange, Hannah Jane Walker) and Rachel Chavkin (The Team).

Title: The Legend of Barney Thomson
Description:
Scotland’s own Robert Carlyle makes his directorial debut with this delightful jet-black comedy about a downtrodden barber whose mundane life is turned upside down when he accidentally turns killer. Carlyle also plays the lead role as mild-mannered Barney Thomson, an old- fashioned barber who is slipping down the pecking order in the Glasgow barber shop where he works. After an accidental killing, he turns to his hilariously fierce mother (a quite wonderful Emma Thompson) for help.
Based on a novel by Douglas Lindsay – the first of seven books about Barney Thomson – the film was shot in Glasgow, with the city a vibrant and vital backdrop to the hilariously black story. Locations include the East End (where the barber shop is located), Shawfield dog track and the Barrowlands, which doubles as the bingo hall where Barney’s controlling mother Cemolina spends quality time. Emma Thompson is a revelation as the mother, complete with Glaswegian accent and a serious amount of make-up to help transform her into a truly memorable character.
The strong cast also includes Ray Winstone (as a fish-out-of-water London copper exasperated by his Scottish police colleagues), Martin Compston (as one of Bobby’s hairdresser rivals) and veteran actor Tom Courtenay (as the police chief baffled by a serial killer who is mailing body parts from a series of different Scottish tourist spots). The Legend of Barney Thomson is a deliriously dark comedy to be cherished...plus, make sure you stay on for the hilarious outtakes over the credit reel.

Title: Walk Two Moons

Utilizing multiple narrative frames, the play leaps back and forth through time and memory as 13-year-old Sal tells the story of the disappearance of her best friend Phoebe’s mother. It is through telling Phoebe’s story that Sal begins to understand why her own mother left and whether or not they’ll ever be together again.

Description: Democracy is a hot topic in Scotland. In last year’s Independence Referendum, many thousands of people even got enthusiastic about it, and the world was watching. Based on the book of the same name, this walking tour takes a gentle uphill path to the top of Calton Hill, with its fabulous views of the city and beyond, to tell a 500-year-old story of democracy, with a spotlight on writers and ideas. We then take a downhill stroll to the Scottish Parliament to bring the story up to the Independence Referendum and beyond.

With great integrity to materials and techniques, and with intellectual rigour and wit, Lichtenstein created visually striking works that continue to provoke questions about how images permeate our lives. 'Visual imagery that sometimes takes the breath away … an experience that will leave no-one who sees it completely unchanged’ (Scotsman). Teaser: Discover the world's most powerful laser in an interactive exhibition, accompanied by events, in the Main Hall of the Scottish Parliament.
Description:
Have you ever wondered how one of the worlds most powerful lasers works? Vulcan is a laser facility  10,000 times more powerful than the National Grid  that can deliver pulses of light of up to one petawatt of energy. A replica of this amazing laser forms the centrepiece of this exhibition, celebrating the International Year of Light 2015, along with interactive exhibits, animations, hardware and displays that tell the story of how lasers impact our daily lives.

The exhibition is accompanied by an exciting events programme of talks and activities for the whole family: hear what a day in the life of a laser scientist is like or get involved in an interactive workshop. Visit scottish.parliament.uk/lasers for the full events programme.

Description: The ‘vivacious ensemble’ (TheArgus.co.uk) Gin and Tonic return with their rendition of this best-loved comedy in a production that once again ‘breathlessly energises Shakespeare’s masterpiece’ **** (BroadwayBaby.com, Hamlet). This crisp adaptation reimagines the story of forbidden relationships and youthful anarchy in a vibrant, modern exploration of lust and love. Sparkling ‘with a confidence not often seen in such a young company’ (BroadwayBaby.com), this hour-long comedy promises to be madly seductive and sizzlingly hot. ‘If you wish to see a Shakespeare play at this year’s Edinburgh Fringe, make it this one.’ **** (Fresh Fringe, Hamlet).

A subversive pilgrimage inspired by the life and works of the trailblazing author, Idiots is an existential parable about the cost of life, humanity and being a speck of dust on the sleeve of the cosmos. Award-winning troupe Caligula's Alibi premiere Idiots, following sell-out runs and critical acclaim. ***** (Scotsman), **** (FestivalJournal.co.uk), **** (BroadwayBaby.com), **** (ThreeWeeks), **** (TheNewCurrent.co.uk), **** (LondonTheatre.co.uk). Expert’s Choice, Stage, Pick of the Week Award, Vault Festival.
Warnings: Adult content, strong language, flashing lights and mild nudity

Join Queen Jesus for a revolutionary queer ritual in which bread is shared, wine is drunk and familiar stories are reimagined by a transgender Jesus. The Guardian’s ‘shows not to miss.’ Featured on BBC Four’s Edinburgh Extra. ‘Reaffirms everyone’s right to live free of discrimination and prejudice’ (Lyn Gardner, Guardian). www.madeinscotlandshowcase.com
Venue description: Summerhall presents The Gospel According to Jesus, Queen of Heaven at St Mark's for 1 night only. A one-off opportunity to see this show in the stunning St Mark's Unitarian Church, transformed each August into a vibrant arts and music venue. Great central setting and performer friendly atmosphere.

Title: Kraftwerk Badger Spaceship

Dominic Berry calls Fat Roland ‘bizarre, astounding, hilarious and truly unlike anyone else’, while the Big Issue in the North calls him ‘funny and highly entertaining’. Peirene Press says his writing is ‘touching, sharp, original and weird’. Judge for yourself in this Fringe debut from a prolific Manchester performer. And mind the badgers. No seriously: when the line dancing finishes, if they move onto the Macarena, we’re stuffed.

A return to pure, full throttle stupid, from comedy’s bestest little dickhead. ‘What your dreams look like when you’ve drunk too much absinthe, and I loved it’ (Times). ‘Sam Simmons' show is a comedy masterpiece’ ***** (Scotsman). Description: Polly Toynbee and David Walker are two of Britain’s leading social democratic commentators and policy analysts. They join Professor Chris Carter to discuss their latest book, Cameron’s Coup, the current political scene, the future for social democracy, and what it’s like to contemplate life at the Guardian newspaper post-Alan Rusbridger. Back by popular demand, this talk is part of the Media Series at the Fringe, where prominent and influential public figures reflect on the current political and media scene. Check our other talks on www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/fringe-media-series.
Venue description: At the heart of a university with a 400 year heritage that is consistently rated one of the world's best, and centrally located in one of Europe's most stunning business and cultural capitals the University of Edinburgh Business School offers an experience that few can rival.

Title: Paula Ryan – Celtic Singer/Songwriter
Description: Paula Ryan is a compelling singer/songwriter from Ireland, whose powerful, insightful songs are inspired by the lyricism and passion of her Gaelic roots and driven by funky rhythmic influences and wacky instruments from other cultures. To accompany her songs, Paula plays marimba, guitar, bazouki, bodhran and djembe. Paula has played at venues and festivals in Ireland, England, Scotland, France, Germany and the USA. Wherever she performs, Paula charms and beguiles audiences with the sheer delight of her music-making, the unmistakeable joy of singing, thought-provoking lyrics and a lively Celtic wit. paularyan.co
Venue description: theSpaceUK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: CeilidhKids at the Fringe – Free!
Description: Family workshop suitable for children aged three to seven years with parents or carers. We involve everyone: skip, clap and march together to traditional Scottish music. Enjoy discovering very simple (often simplified) dances that you might find at a ceilidh or Scottish country dance, celebrating the social aspects of dancing with a partner. CeilidhKids is all about fun for all generations. Hugely popular with local families, now it's your turn.
Warnings: All children should be accompanied by an adult willing to join in. Gorgie City Farm sessions are weather-dependent.

Title: Fashion And The Selfie Culture
Description: Mal Burkinshaw, Programme Director of Fashion at Edinburgh College of Art and Director of the Diversity Network discusses and debates the role that fashion plays in stereotyping ideals of beauty – when are we ever good enough? With the rise of the me, me, me selfie culture – why do we succumb to pressure to present an image of ourselves to the world that is not the image we see in the mirror, or the image beneath the skin? This show asks whether empathy can ever change the strict doctrines of current beauty codes.
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.

Title: Will Gompertz
Subtitle: Embrace Your Creativity and Improve Your Life?
Description: BBC arts editor Will Gompertz has interviewed plenty of creative people. In Think Like an Artist he focuses not just on their output, but the creativity with which they approach their work. He argues that there’s a link between creativity and entrepreneurialism, and using artists like Picasso and Warhol as examples, he says we can improve our own lives by learning some of their skills.

Title: Niall Campbell & Blake Morrison
Subtitle: Shimmering Poetry
Description: The potent sea broods as a backdrop to these two shimmering poetry collections. Niall Campbell’s Moontide is a multi awarding-winning debut that signals a major new voice on the Scottish poetry scene. Meanwhile it’s 28 years since bestselling memoirist and novelist Blake Morrison’s last full poetry collection, but Shingle Street, inspired by the eroding Suffolk coastline, confirms that his voice is as powerfully assured as ever.

Title: Under Flat Sky / Edge of Nowhere
Description: Under Flat Sky is a stunningly beautiful immersion of dancers in a moving visual art landscape specially made by German artist Silke Mansholt. Commissioned by the Museum of Art Kochi in Japan, the work is lyrical with Butoh influences accompanied by the extraordinary vocals of Rowan Godel. Edge of Nowhere is a playful solo choreographed by Billy Cowie for Indian dancer Rajyashree Ramamurthi. The Odissi influenced dances combine elements of storytelling, gesture and facial expression accompanied by violin, harmonium, piano and tablas.
Venue description: Dance Base is a National Centre for Dance housed in an award-winning and fully-accessible venue in the heart of the historic old town. We celebrate the potential for dance in everyone with year-round professional and community activity. We present an exciting and Fringe-friendly programme from Scotland, Wales, Ireland, Italy, Poland, US, Taiwan and New Zealand. This year we have 4 spaces including a Secret Garden and professional classes during August.

Title: Anthony Sattin
Subtitle: Time for TE
Description: In 1914, the man who would become Lawrence of Arabia destroyed a manuscript which he’d written, telling of his childhood and twenties. Anthony Sattin, author of several travel and history books, has unearthed the dramatic story of T E Lawrence’s birth, the deeply difficult relationship he had with his mother, and the personal reasons which triggered his journey from student to spy. Chaired by Stuart Kelly.

Title: Don't F*ck with Me Gweilo: Stories from a World Citizen
Description: International Comedian and British job thief Dana Alexander is back with her fourth Edinburgh Show. Since immigrating to Britain over four years ago and touring in nearly 30 countries Miss Alexander has amassed a healthy amount of tales from around the world. Watching the explosion of nationalism compete with globalisation, all the while wondering if we can find a common ground. Why can't I go anywhere on planet earth without someone asking me where I am from? And why is black face still acceptable in Holland.
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and late comers may not be admitted.

Title: Bold Girls
Description: Bold Girls is a dark comedy about the friendship of four women living in the midst of war-torn Belfast. Rona Munro’s play looks at the ways in which the troubles shaped their lives as they tried to survive and at the fragility of their dreams in such volatile times. Marie, Cassie and Nora try desperately to maintain normality, even after everything they have known has changed – but an unexpected visitor arrives and the women begin to question everything they thought they knew.
Artist: New Celts Productions and Laughing Hen Productions

A must for nurses or anyone who ever needed one. Sold out season and Best Comedy nomination, Perth Fringe 2015. Sold out season and Best Emerging Comedy nomination, Adelaide Fringe 2013. Adelaide Comedian of the Year 2012. RAW National finalist 2012. 'Carroll is really very funny … effortless … delivers a sharp, pointed anecdote' (Heckler.com.au).

Title: Physics to Blow Your Mind
Teaser: Join a top astronomer and a leading astrophysicist for a curious journey through some of the most mysterious and intriguing secrets of the cosmos.
Description: Physics to Blow your Mind is back! Join a top astronomer and a leading astrophysicist for a curious journey through some of the most mysterious and intriguing secrets of the cosmos. Theoretical astrophysicist Dr Katherine Freese will ponder what the universe made of, the longest outstanding problem in all of modern physics and the most important research topic in cosmology and particle physics today. Astronomer Dr Jacqueline Mitton will then look into the origin and evolution of our solar system, which may one day provide answers to the mystery of the origin of life on Earth.

Title: Amazing Immunology
Teaser: Reveal the secrets of your immune system in a fun interactive session with real medical research scientists.
Description: Reveal the secrets of your immune system in a fun interactive session where you'll explore allergies, infections and vaccinations with real medical research scientists. Help Denny and the T-Team find and solve 3D puzzles, try the Rash Decisions ball pool challenge and complete your Immunological Stickers story. For ages 6-11.

Title: Inverkeithing Community Big Band
Description: Join Fife’s biggest, most fabulous big band for a sumptuous afternoon of classic tunes from Count Basie to Maynard Ferguson. With swinging saxes, raunchy brass, sexy grooves, and featuring vocalists Benita Baugh and Tom Marshall.  With guest artist Richard Ingham.

Title: Nordic Raga Trio
Description: Nordic Raga Trio is an inspired meeting between one Indian and two Swedish folk musicians, who want to experiment with bringing more improvisation into Nordic folk music. To find inspiration for this they use models for how improvisation is used in classical Indian music. In a typical Nordic Raga concert the emphasis is on improvised music, but the band also performs both more traditional Nordic and Carnatic music. 'Swedish waltzes and polskas meet Bangalore passion, grace and fire in this superb communion' (Herald, Fringe 2014). Jyotsna Srikanth (violin), Pär Moberg (wind instruments), Dan Svensson (percussion, vocals).
Venue description: Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is approx 5 - 10 minutes' walk from the important Haymarket road and rail interchange.

Description: The Lost and the Found by Cat Clarke is a disturbing account of the abduction of 6 year old Laurel. Thirteen years later a teenage girl turns up, disorientated and clutching Laurel's old teddy. In Blackfin Sky Kat Ellis tells the tale of Skylar, who falls from Blackfin Pier and drowns. Three months later she reappears as if nothing has happened. Secrets, lies and broken realities by two exceptional writers.

Title: The Labour Of Laugh
Description: The Labour Of Laugh features the cracks in careers and the jokes in jobs, including incompetence, time wasters, blaggers and more. If you have a job, have had a job, or plan to get a job you will love it. 'Sam is a very funny man' (Carl Donnelly). 'I love Sam's laid back observations, interspersed with mad links and thoughts' (Sadie Nine, BBC Essex).

SE:UM continue the traditions of ethnic Korean music, but are also aware they are living in the 21st century, as they immerse themselves in modern music. Traditional sounds are mixed with jazz, folk, and freeform style to create an entirely new and exciting fusion. With its auditory and visual spectacle, this exotic experience has received increasing acclaim from audiences worldwide. Don't miss this unique opportunity to witness one of Korea's top fusion bands.

Description: Award-winning stand-up comic Ashley Storrie performs her debut solo show at the Free Festival. From gigs in LA, to an award-winning podcast and BBC Radio pilot under her belt she is set to storm the Fringe. With painfully funny extracts from her teen diaries and hilariously honest accounts of her less than normal life this Tall Storrie has to be seen to be believed. ‘Witty and intelligent’ (BroadwayBaby.com). ‘An experienced and accomplished comic ... isn't afraid to frighten the front row with brutally funny material’ (Scotsman).

Title: Brand New-U
Description: Acclaimed documentary-maker Simon Pummell makes his drama debut with Brand New-U, a stylish and astutely complex sci-fi thriller about Slater (Lachlan Nieboer) who will do anything he can to follow Nadia (Nora-Jane Noone), the love of his life. When she vanishes, his only clue is shadowy company Brand new-U, which deals in new personalities. he makes a deal with the operation, but when the borders between his identities clash, his obsessive quest becomes dangerous.

Title: This Will End Badly

Title: Patrick Gale
Subtitle: You Can Escape, But Will You Find Yourself?
Description: Much loved for his bestselling novels set in Cornwall, Patrick Gale’s work takes an exciting new turn in A Place Called Winter. The novel brilliantly evokes the harsh landscapes of the Canadian prairie for those who emigrated from Britain to make their lives there. This warm-hearted, devastating story has an added twist: it’s the breathtaking fictionalised tale of Gale’s own great-grandfather.

Title: Imran Yusuf: Super Roar of the Underdog Turbo X: HD Remix
Description: Star of brand new BBC Three sitcom Fried and CBBC’s Ultimate Brain, Best Newcomer nominee Imran Yusuf returns with a special edition show of his latest, cutting edge socio-political stand-up that’s nothing short of starting a movement! Join Imran as he puts the world to rights whilst deftly defeating all prejudices with his cheeky charm, calling out the bullshit and bringing people together against the renaissance of bigotry that threatens to take us into a dark age. Come join the revolution, it starts here! ‘Sharp, passionate, uplifting.’ **** (Telegraph)

Title: The Wonderful Imagination of Oliver Jeffers
Description: Writer and illustrator Oliver Jeffers’ work is a definite favourite on bookshelves the world over. Lost and Found, How to Catch a Star and The Incredible Book Eating Boy are en route to modern classic status. Join him to hear all about his latest off the wall tale The Day the Crayons Came Home. A very funny, joyfully illustrated story that shows crayons have feelings too so don’t lose, break or melt them!

Title: My First Laugh
Description: A comedy show about comedy. Ever wondered how comedians started? Ever wondered what their first joke was. This show answers it all. Famous and established acts talk about their genesis and revisit their first ever comedy set.
Artist: Nigel Lovell/Oh So Funny/PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: We are an Edinburgh City Centre Sports Bar, Diner and Nightclub located just behind Waverly Station. Whether you're after watching one of our 40 screens (including two projectors) to see your favorite sport, or to sit and have a meal in our restaurant area upstairs, or just to come in for a refreshing pint or cocktail, Sportsters can offer it all!!! Drinks Promos offered all week round! 18+ http://edinburgh.sportsters.info/

Title: Molly Antopol & Eliza Robertson
Subtitle: Seismic International Talents
Description: US author Molly Antopol and Canadian Eliza Robertson are among a wave of young short story writers taking North American literature in new directions. Antopol’s debut collection, The UnAmericans, unfolds in Belarus, Tel Aviv and NYC's Upper West Side. Meanwhile, a woman in one of Eliza Robertson’s grippingly tense stories from Wallflowers proclaims weirdly, ‘I feel love in the backs of my eyes’.

Title: Gary Busey's One-Man Hamlet as Performed by David Carl
Description: Having triumphed in Celebrity Big Brother, survived Celebrity Rehab with Dr. Drew and battled with Meatloaf and Donald Trump, Keanu Reeves' favourite co-star now takes on his biggest challenge yet: performing all the parts in Hamlet at the Edinburgh Fringe, with songs and homemade puppets – anything could happen! Written by David Carl (after Shakespeare), co-created and directed by Michole Biancosino. Outstanding Solo Performance award winner, Fringe NY 2014. 'It's crazy hilarious' **** Critics’ Pick (Time Out NY). Mega-Top Pick (BestNewYorkComedy.com). 'So demented a concept, it actually works' (New York Post).

Brothers Famous Seamus and Sean-tastic will do anything to be famous, really anything! If you're lucky you might even end up in Sean's adopted family! Charm, sharp wit, and good humour with flashes of acrobatic skills and just enough naughtiness to keep kids and adults guessing. Silly and bonkers – absolutely bonkers! Come and enjoy spectacular circus, hilarious cabaret, raucous music or an enchanting children's show in one of our beautiful Spiegeltents. Title: Dead Rising: Watchtower
Description: A slick and bloodily amusing film spin-off from the Dead Rising video game, set in the fictional city of East Mission, Oregon, where the authorities have created Zombrex, a vaccine that delays the effects of the infection. In the middle of the zombie mayhem is reporter Chase Carter (Jesse Metcalfe, Desperate Housewives) who teams with kick-ass Crystal O'Rourke (an impressive Meghan Ory) to fend off the walking dead and also try and escape the closed down city. A strong cast also includes Virginia Madsen and Dennis Haysbert.

Title: A Translation of Shadows
Description: Have you ever fallen in love with a film star? Have they loved you back? In Japan Benshi were live narrators of silent films until the ‘talkies’ wiped them out. Now, thanks to internationally acclaimed theatre mavericks Stan’s Cafe shooting their own silent film in Tokyo, the Benshi is back! In A Translation of Shadows he narrates Shadows, telling the story of the film and its fictional cast. Inevitably he’s in love with the leading lady. When she shows no sign of loving him back he foolishly decides he can change the story.
Venue description: Summerhall presents engaging, challenging, high-quality theatre, dance, literature, visual art and music for people of all ages.  Our unique home in the former Dick Vet building of the University of Edinburgh offers atmospheric performance spaces, a buzzy courtyard and an onsite pub, the Royal Dick Bar, with something for everyone to explore, discover and enjoy - “an entire festival in its own right” The Guardian
Venue accessibility:

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café.
We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please do not hesitate to contact us by phone on 0845 874 3000 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

http://www.summerhall.co.uk/about/accessibility/. Ramp access is at the side of the venue on Summerhall Square.

Title: Max and Ivan: The End
Description: Welcome to Sudley-on-Sea. Take a look around. You don't have long. Seriously. Foster's Edinburgh Comedy Award and Melbourne Barry Award nominees Max and Ivan (BBC One's W1A, BBC Radio 4's Casebook of Max and Ivan) return to the Edinburgh Fringe to tell an epic narrative sketch comedy tale about the hopes, fears and dreams of a doomed town. Directed by Tom Parry (Pappy's). 'Max and Ivan are the real deal' **** (Guardian). **** (Times). **** (Independent). **** (Time Out). **** (Chortle.co.uk). 'Undoubtedly superstars of tomorrow' (GQ).
Artist: Mick Perrin Worldwide in association with Dawn Sedgwick Management
Venue description: Since 2000 the Pleasance Dome has been the hub of the now-famous Bristo Square, with the best comedy and theatre in 5 venues all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late in to the night.

Title: LateLab: Pecha Kucha
Teaser: PechaKucha Night is a presentation format that is based on a simple idea: 20 images x 20 seconds. Start the clock...
Description:
PechaKucha Night was devised in Tokyo in February 2003 as an event for young designers to meet, network and show their work in public. It has turned into a massive celebration, with events happening in hundreds of cities around the world, inspiring creatives worldwide. Drawing its name from the Japanese term for the sound of 'chit chat', it rests on a presentation format that is based on a simple idea: 20 images x 20 seconds. Start the clock...

LateLab is a collaboration between Edinburgh International Science Festival and New Media Scotland.

Title: Bob Doolally Football Legend
Description: The legendary retired football manager, turned alcoholic pundit from hell is back from his fact-finding mission to Qatar, and still talking balls. Expect some outrageous views on football, some random filth and plenty of drink-fuelled rage on life in general. Plus Bob’s now legendary question and answer session. Any question may be asked, any answer will be given. A Fringe favourite every year since 1998 – sadly the last time Scotland actually qualified for the World Cup! ‘Foul-mouthed and politically-incorrect’ (Scotsman). ‘Razor-sharp observations of the British psyche' (Guardian). 'Almost better than football' (Independent).
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.
Venue description: Across the road from the original venue Stand 1, Stand 3 is a superb large theatre space with its own bar, and Stand 4 an intimate studio with exciting Fringe debuts. Venues accessible through courtyard at basement level.

Title: Fourth Monkey's Grimm Tales: The Bloody Countess
Description: ‘An immersive, midnight spectacle’ **** (AYoungerTheatre.com). ‘Theatre at its most inventive’ **** (Stage). Following the sell-out success of Alice in 2014, Fourth Monkey return to the Fringe with another late night treat for the fainthearted. Descended from one of the most aristocratic families in Europe, Erzsebet Bathory became known as the most sadistic female serial killer in history. Torturing and slaughtering an estimated 650 young women and bathing in the spilt blood of the murdered virgins to preserve her youth. An epic tale of gothic decadence.
Venue description: theSpaceUK presents this brand new state of the art facility over 3 floors. Located next door to theSpace @ Surgeons Hall and  theSpace @ Symposium Hall we  present an unrivalled and diverse programme in seven performance spaces. Dance, Drumming, Circus, Physical,  Music, Theatre, Choral, Interactive, Immersive, Sketch, Cabaret and Spoken Word makes this a unique central hub at the very heart of the modern Edinburgh Festival Fringe.

Title: Lorna Reid: All of Me
Description: Heartfelt jazz, blues and Americana, Lorna and her musicians perform beautiful standards from the great American songbook. Also, originals from her acclaimed album Falling Like Dew and new single My Hotel Wrecking Days Are Over. Regularly played on national radio, the cool and classy vocalist has shades of Ella, Billie Holiday, Linda Ronstadt and Diana Krall. Lorna, one of Scotland’s most sought after performers, has been described as 'one of Scotland’s most talented singer-songwriters' (MusicNewsScotland.wordpress.com). 'Tasteful, elegant, soulful' (Scotsman). 'This show manages to be simultaneously warm and very cool' (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: This stylish basement bar is Edinburgh's coolest, quintuple award-winning, year-round live music venue, with a crammed daily programme of multi-genre music and Fringe shows running all day, every day, from 13:00-05:00. As well as all the independent Fringe shows hosted by the venue, you’ll hear the bar’s own programme of excellent music, with great jazz, funk, acoustic, blues and rocky sounds – and bar service to 05:00 nightly!

Title: The Oxford Revue: Issues
Description: The critically acclaimed Oxford Revue returns to the Fringe for its 51st year, bringing an hour of hilarious sketch comedy, written and performed by the country's finest student comedians. Mixing the absurd and the satirical, Issues promises to be the Revue's sharpest and most subversive show to date. Since it was founded, the Oxford Revue has been the starting point for many of the UK's best loved comedians, including Rowan Atkinson, Alan Bennett and Michael Palin. 'Witty, inventive and extremely clever' ***** (ThreeWeeks).

Teaser: A hands-on, family-friendly session with activities, storytelling and interactive displays about the lives of farm animals.
Description: A hands-on, family-friendly session with activities, storytelling and interactive displays about the lives of farm animals. Moredun scientists show and tell how they help control pests and diseases, which leads to healthier and happier sheep, cows, pigs and chickens, and is better for the environment.

Title: Photosynthesis
Description: The first exhibition in Scotland by artists from the Dutch art collective Tropism. Featuring photographs of plants taken with unusual, often scientific, visualisation techniques, the exhibition provides a surprising and spectacularly different view on plants. Botanical installations located around the Garden will fuse art, poetry and science and combine audio, video and classic museum displays. The Tropists are a group of artists that work with phenomena occurring at the edge of perception: events that are hardly noticed, but which lead to a reaction similar to the manner in which a plant responds to light.
Venue: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh – John Hope Gateway
Venue description: The John Hope Gateway is a shining example of green construction and sustainability, offering a range of exhibitions and event spaces, restaurant and the Botanics Shop.

Title: All Our Friends Are Dead
Description: Dark and anarchic sketches full of twisted characters, satirical songs and close to the bone tragicomedy. 'A relentless hour of fast and furious comedy' ***** (GoodReview.co.uk). 'The bizarre isolationists, the power crazed, the sublimated, the sexually confused and more...' ***** (Skinny). 'Take two talented writers and actresses whose minds have been warped, let them loose on a stage and prepare for laughter' **** (PublicReviews.com). 'Surreal, fun and frankly pretty ridiculous' **** (WhatsOnStage.com). And join Norris and Parker themselves as they struggle through their quarter life crisis unable to buy cheese, dignity and other luxury items.
Warnings: Buy a ticket in advance to guarantee entry or Pay What You Want at the venue.

Title: David Gates & Thomas Morris
Subtitle: Stories in the Spirit of Raymond Carver
Description: A Pulitzer Prize finalist for his novel Jernigan, New York-based David Gates creates irresistible anti-heroes who feel like grown up versions of Holden Caulfield. His new stories describe the hopes and disappointments of such characters in the North-East of the USA. Meanwhile the Dublin-based Welshman Thomas Morris builds his fearsomely-accomplished debut story collection, We Don’t Know What We’re Doing, around characters in his home town of Caerphilly.

Spotlites has a repuation for quality five and four star sell-outs, clean facilities and caring, helpful staff.

Teaser: Easter science shenanigans with the world's favourite TV stunt scientist, Dr Bunhead.

Title: The Sino Profusion Show
Description: Performed by Shanghai's Hand in Hand Troupe, a famous young artists' association in China. The troupe, delegated by the City of Shanghai government, visited and performed in the USA, France, Germany, Italy and other countries, giving performances described as excellent and extraordinary, and the artists were regarded as muses of international friendship. The show ranges from joyous Han dance, to classical, and from Dai minority dance to Uygur minority dance. This brilliant performance will bring a highlight to the Edinburgh Fringe, as well as a new understanding of Chinese minority culture.

If you only see one show this Fringe, then please, please, take her with you? She loves meeting new people! Leicester New Comedian of the Year 2015 nominee. Title: Sherry & The Mystery of Palo Cortado (Jerez & El Misterio Del Palo Cortado)
Description:
Sherry was once Spain's most important export, but its perception has changed over the years and it is not seen as the versatile wine it actually is. The film leaves you keen to taste as you learn the difference between oloroso, fino and amontillado; and draws you into the rare and subtle taste of a Palo Cortado (a type of sherry whose spontaneous oxidation creates a rare taste), defined by its deeper colouring and balance of sweet and dry. History, taste and culture all provide the backdrop to this intriguing documentary.
Doc of the Day
The screening on 23 June is our Doc of the Day and there will be a Q&A post screening with director José Luis López-Linares and producer Antonio Saura. You can also partake in Sherry tasting and enjoy some iberico ham.

Title: Eureka! Ancient Greece and its brilliant scientific discoveries
Teaser: A celebration of science from Ancient Greece through interactive storytelling with soft hand puppets.
Description: A celebration of science from Ancient Greece as Carolyne Latham and her friendly little dog invite you to travel in time and discover the stories behind the science. The whole family will enjoy this gentle introduction to the wonders of the ancient world through interactive storytelling with soft hand puppets. You'll meet one of the earliest scientists, join in with a favourite animal fable and visit the first ever Olympic Games.

Title: Ivo Graham: No Filter
Description: Album three (The Queen is Dead, OK Computer, etc) from Graham after 2014's 'joyous show' (Evening Standard), and this year there's apparently a bit more bite to the boy's bark. Can this be true? Definitely worth investigating. As seen/heard on BBC Three's Edinburgh Comedy Fest Live, and Sweat the Small Stuff; Comedy Central's Live At The Comedy Store; BBC Radio 5 live's Fighting Talk; and XFM's Josh Widdicombe show. Description: An original comedy written and performed by real life brother and sister. Horrids is the shop of dreams until two useless berks begin to work there. Olivia Nixon is a comedy actress known for her work with BBC Radio 4, and Luke Nixon (despite being the younger sibling) has already picked up a four-star review from his first play at the 2014 Edinburgh Fringe. Title: Al Porter Is Yours
Description: Al Porter Is Yours is the irreverent debut show from Ireland's newest comedy star. At 22, Al falls in love daily, has 'completed' Tinder and is still a mammy's boy! A parish secretary's son, Al was supposed to be a priest – until he slept with one and changed his mind. A socialite on a social welfare budget, Al has been on countless dates, gotten into debt and was sued by a presidential candidate! In this candid hour he pours over the details of it all in his playful style that's been described as council-estate camp.

Description: Beautifully remastered and looking as glorious as when it was first released, this 1949 classic stars Joseph Cotten as pulp novelist Holly Martins who travels to post-war Vienna and starts to investigate the mysterious death of his old friend, black-marketeer Harry Lime. Memorable thanks to the famous first glimpse of Lime (Orson Welles), Robert Krasker’s black-and-white cinematography, the chase through the sewers, the cuckoo clock speech, and Anton Karas’ zither music.

Title: Sweeney Todd: The Panto
Description: After 15 years in exile, famed barber Sweeney Todd returns to London in search of his wife Lucy. Little does he realise that she has been captured by the villainous Judge Turpin. Can Sweeney rescue her from his grasp? And what is the secret behind the curvaceous Mrs Lovett's pie shop? With a razor sharp wit and apologies to Stephen Sondheim, Sweeney Todd: The Panto is a bloody good time!

Description: Widely regarded as one of the leading young companies in the UK, Newbury Youth Theatre have an unparalleled reputation at the Edinburgh Fringe. They have presented an original production here for sixteen consecutive years and have consistently garnered four- and five-star reviews. This new production of Hilaire Belloc’s darkly comic stories is told with their trademark style of rambunctious storytelling, original songs and touches of simple magic. Tom Drury is a US novelist who wrote his debut novel, The End of Vandalism, back in 1994. In the States it has gradually come to be regarded as a comic classic. Now, at last, it is released in the UK.

Title: Le nozze di Figaro
Description: Join Opera dei Lumi for a performance of Mozart’s vivacious comedy Le nozze di Figaro. Mozart’s glorious score effortlessly drives the plot's rollercoaster mix of vivacious humour, sexual intrigue, mistaken identity and unexpected revelation towards a touching finale of forgiveness and joy. Opera dei Lumi are a new Scottish-based company specialising in the performance of opera from the Enlightenment period and drawing upon talent across Britain and Europe. Experience Mozart's masterpiece on your own terms through this innovatively presented semi-staged performance, drawing on the music as the driving dramatic force rather than relying on the staging.

Title: Black Box Shorts 3: The Price of Progress
Description:
Soon
Jeanne Liotta/USA/2014/7 min/European premiere
The most current Greenland and CO2 data visualisations are used to consider the ongoing state of melting Arctic sea ice due to the warming of air and oceans caused by carbon emissions.
Into the Great White Open
Michaela Grill/Austria, Canada/2015/16 min/International premiere
Shifting and gliding views of the Arctic Ocean oscillate between abstraction and figuration. Snow, ice, clouds, and pixels melt and collide, confusing our sense of spatial orientation.
The Atom Station
Nick Jordan/UK/2015/13 min/World premiere
The battle between nature and industry is at the centre of this documentary about the exploitation of Icelandic landscapes for economic gain. With two contrasting voice-overs by poet WH Auden and environmental activist Ómar Ragnarsson.
Quiet Zone
David Bryant, Karl Lemieux/Canada/2015/14 min/UK premiere
Interviews with women who suffer from electromagnetic sensitivity are brought together with chemically treated film imagery, rendering physical and tangible this elusive modern phenomenon.
sound of a million insects, light of a thousand stars
Tomonari Nishikawa/Japan/2014/2 min/UK premiere
35mm negative film stock was buried under leaves near the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station. The abstract flurry of activity on the surface of the filmstrip translates the energies of the radioactive site.
Gasometers Pt2
Nicky Hamlyn/UK/2015/14 min/World premiere
Part of a series of visual studies of gas holders in North London that draws out the ambiguous status of these majestic historic constructions.
vindmøller
Margaret Rorison/USA/2014/3 min/UK premiere
A textural exploration of a landscape scattered with wind turbines in Copenhagen. Multiple exposures of a roll of colour film, along with acoustic resonances, translate the eerie atmosphere of these iconic structures.
The Devastated Land (Le Pays Dévasté)
Emmanuel Lefrant/France/2015/12 min/UK premiere
Through a series of painstaking material interventions, Lefrant constructs a landscape where human dominance over the environment - defined as the age of the Anthropocene - is starkly visualised.

This documentary is the previously untold story of a post-punk/indie music scene that reverberated from Edinburgh, throughout the UK and beyond.

Title: Ambush with Chris Bradford
Description: Chris Bradford has gone to extreme lengths to prepare himself for writing his books, including training in Samurai swordmanship and becoming a black belt in Zen Kyu Shin Taijutsu. Now he has embarked on an intensive close protection course to become a qualified professional bodyguard. Join Chris with the latest instalment of his bestselling Bodyguard series, Ambush, which takes a teenage martial arts expert into the heart of Africa.

Title: North Sea Gas: Scottish Spirit
Description: Edinburgh's award-winning band return to the AMC for the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, with songs and stories from their latest album, Fire in the Glen and from previous recordings. They will entertain you in the Scottish Spirit with an array of instruments, tremendous three-part harmonies and great craic. ‘They remain naturally at home on the folk club and village hall circuit as they are on the bigger stages, expertly working in plenty of deadpan pawky humour’ (Scotsman).
Venue description: Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is approx 5 - 10 minutes' walk from the important Haymarket road and rail interchange.
Venue accessibility: Induction loop in Big Room and in venue box office but not in Back Room. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Title: Complete Brahms Symphonies
Description: The Orchestra of the Canongait and its conductor, Robert Dick, have been developing an enviable reputation over the past few years for the quality of their performances of some of the largest scale works in the entire symphonic repertoire, including the towering masterpieces of Bruckner, Mahler and Richard Strauss. For the 2015 Fringe, they present a unique opportunity to hear one of the greatest symphonic cycles in all music, the four symphonies of Johannes Brahms. Unmissable! For further details, visit www.canongait.org. 'The climaxes were shattering in their power' (BachTrack.com review of 2013 performance of Bruckner's Ninth Symphony).
Venue description: Founded in 1620, Greyfriars Kirk is an iconic building situated in the heart of Scotland's capital.  Also situated at the centre of the Fringe Festival venues it is a beautiful and atmospheric space for worship, choral and orchestral works.  The Kirk has a magnificent acoustic and during 2015 the congregation is celebrating the 25th anniversary of the Collins organ with a festival of worship and the arts.

Title: Under the Ground
Description: A brand new musical following the seemingly simple journey of a girl on a single Glasgow Subway car. Forced to face her fears and overcome private demons on this very public platform, surrounded with characters on journeys of their own. Under the Ground explores the phenomenon of loneliness on a train packed with strangers, stories and secrets.
Venue description: Assembly Checkpoint is the Fringe's premier venue for cabaret, music and more. The venue is located inside an old church and exudes warmth and charm. There is a bar inside the upstairs venue and further drinking and dining options downstairs.

Title: Celebrity Organ Recitals 2015-4
Description: Michael Harris, organist of St Giles’ Cathedral, puts the world-renowned Rieger organ in St Giles' through its paces, with music including JS Bach Prelude and Fugue in G BWV 541, Ritter Sonata No 3 in A, and Dupré Prelude and Fugue in B major.
Venue description: Founded in the 1120s, St Giles' was the church of John Knox during the Reformation and is renowned for its stained glass, Rieger organ and beautiful Thistle Chapel. Open daily. Free guided tours, concerts and shop. Donations welcome. For access and prices to the newly opened Roof and Tower Tours check website.

Title: Live Roller Derby Presented by Auld Reekie Roller Girls
Description: The best skaters in Scotland will pit their wits and hits against each other as Edinburgh showcases full-contact, all-female roller derby. Families are welcome to watch this test of strength, speed and agility as skaters battle through their rival’s team using only the power of their bodies. Hosts Auld Reekie Roller Girls will join forces with other Scottish leagues to showcase this unique sport in what promise to be an exciting, action-packed evening.
Venue description: Meadowbank Sports Centre is situated in central Edinburgh and comprises a 25-acre complex of indoor and outdoor facilities. The centre can accommodate sporting and art and entertainment from local to international level, including exhibitions, conferences, meetings and concerts.

Title: The HandleBards: A Midsummer Night's Dream
Description: Touring the UK, carrying all set, props, costumes on just four bicycles, the HandleBards play all 21 characters in this all-male production of Shakespeare's woodland spectacle. Pack a picnic and join us in the Botanic Gardens. The HandleBards do Shakespeare differently. Reaching the Fringe after a 1,500 mile cycle from London, performing with eight very sore legs, the four 'Bards present a fast-paced farce of Shakespeare's best-loved play. 'An unmissable show' ***** (BroadwayBaby.com on Macbeth, 2014). 'It's back to basics storytelling in the best way' **** (WhatsOnStage.com on The Comedy of Errors, 2014). www.handlebards.com
Warnings: This performance is outdoors. Please bring a chair or blanket to sit on, and dress for the weather.
Venue: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh – West Gate
Venue description: The Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh is a unique setting for outdoor performances, with spectacular views across the city skyline.

Title: Rory McSwiggan Wants Nothing to Do With Himself
Description: His parents and teachers told him it was rude to brag about giving money to charity or saving children from drowning. But Rory grew up to find that nobody else, especially people born after 1987, thought or acted in this way. He set about telling stories that inadvertently related to his life, in a stand-up comedy format. You may be able to relate. ‘Bloody good comedian’ (Hobgoblin Comedy). ‘A wonderful way with words’ (Voicebox Comedy, Belfast).

With the bank due to auction her house she must beg and borrow money at all costs, leading to moments of real suspense punctuated an unexpected dash of dark humour.

Title: Aunty Donna
Description: Aussie Edinburgh favourites return with a killer new show. Unique, tight, fresh, filthy, but best of all flat out, laugh 'til your face hurts funny. Hold onto your seats, don't blink! You won't want to miss a beat. Expect 60 minutes of pure sketch comedy that transports you into the warped world that is Aunty Donna – turning the ridiculous into the sublime. 'Comparable to some glorious crossbreed of The Mighty Boosh and Flight of the Conchords ... appreciation and split sides were universal' ***** (BroadwayBaby.com). 'Ingenious and brilliantly crafted ... smart, fast-paced, hilarious and wonderfully absurd’ (List).
Warnings: Mild/strong language
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces and seven bars including the exclusive roof top bar, The Loft. A must for all Fringe-goers. Description: What's in your strangest sandwich? Where's my glue I have no clue? Poems, wordplay and joining in for children 4-10 and their families. Writer-performer Rachel Sambrooks was an Artist in Residence for SPINE Festival 2015, has had her work broadcast on BBC Radio, has recently published The Strangest Sandwich in the World as her first collection of children's poems. www.rachelsambrooks.com

Title: BEASTS: Live DVD
Description: Big time sketch heroes BEASTS are returning to Edinburgh to film a live DVD of their best ever show. Audience needed, also camera. Total sell-out 2013 and 2014. Book now to avoid lifelong regret. As heard on BBC Radio 4. Directed by Tom Parry (Pappy's). 'Unforgettably nutty' **** (Times). 'Delightfully entertaining' **** (Telegraph). 'Pure, unabashed silliness' **** (Metro). 'The new breed of sketch show' (Guardian).
Venue description: Soak up the legendary atmosphere at the Pleasance Courtyard, considered by many to be the heart of the Fringe. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Description: Ben Fogg (self-proclaimed ninth funniest man alive, both halves of the original odd couple, Mr Oak Furniture Land 2009, close personal friend of Avril Lavigne) has written a deep, rich walrus of a show. Joke topics include: Taylor Swift, late night shopping, hotel breakfasts, true love, fake love, and leaves. Dress code: business casual. 'If you don’t love it you can kick me square in the nuts' (Ben Fogg).
Venue description: Fringe Venue 462

Title: Jura Unbound
Subtitle: Trading Stories
Description: Jura Unbound 2015 takes flight with a night of seductive international short stories. Join us on our journey with Denmark’s Dorthe Nors, author of Karate Chop; Ireland’s Mary Costello reading from her debut collection, The China Factory, USA’s Molly Antopol whose collection is The UnAmericans; David Gates, whose A Hand Reached Down to Guide Me, is his first book for a decade; and Mexican author Adriana Díaz Enciso, who reads an extract from her novel Odio. Just to make the evening even more special we have music from Fife’s alt-folk mainstay James Yorkston.

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: Love is a Human Right
Description: We all have the right to be treated as equals, regardless of our gender identity or sexuality. But being lesbian, gay, bisexual, transsexual or intersex is a crime in many countries. Amnesty is campaigning for a world where no one faces this kind of discrimination. In this event we hear the work of writers persecuted for their sexuality. Reading today: Margie Orford, Edward Mendelson, Ziauddin Sardar and David Roberts.

Title: Japan Marvelous Drummers
Description: Having performed in over 20 countries across the globe, Japan Marvelous Drummers’ eight performers use the traditional instruments of Japan including drums of all sizes, the Koto harp, bamboo flutes and clarinet to create a truly unique show. Combining the power of these instruments with dance, humour and beauty, this intense rhythmic show has the power to change the way you think about Japan forever. ‘This musical extravaganza displays phenomenal strength, co-ordination and stamina. A true spectacle of Japanese music’ ***** (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: Assembly George Square Theatre is perfectly located next to Assembly George Square Gardens and Studios for pre or post show drinks or food. The theatre itself is a purpose built venue with comfortable modern seating for up to 500, while the The Box is an intimate 80 seat studio hosting great theatre and comedy.

Title: Old Saint Paul's Festival Masses
Description: Traditional Catholic Anglican liturgy in this historic church close to Edinburgh's Royal Mile with renowned choir and organ. Directed by City and University Organist John Kitchen. Service music will include Masses by Victoria (O Quam Gloriosum), Andrew Carter (Missa Sancti Pauli), Howells (Collegium Regale). Complete details of service music from www.osp.org.uk or venue leaflet.
Venue description: Historic Anglican church in the Catholic tradition, one of the original homes of Scottish Episcopacy, founded in 1689. The hidden gem of the Old Town, with numerous features of architectural and artistic interest. Father Willis organ. Descriptive leaflets available. Open daily 08:30-17:45 to visit, or for peace and stillness.

Title: Kayfabe
Description: Hosts of the Time Out Critics’ Choice show Character Assassination, Simon Lukacs (‘Incredibly charming’ FunnyWomen.com) and Lola-Rose Maxwell bring their debut character hour, Kayfabe, to the Fringe. Expect snooker-obsessed erotic novelists, demented butterflies, and more in an hour of silly, surreal and sharp comedy. Together, Lola and Simon are part of The Petting Zoo (‘Improv supergroup’ Time Out) and separately can be seen in Demons to Some, Equine Extravaganza and the 2014 Edinburgh smash Upstairs Downton (***** EdinburghGuide.com).
Venue description: An Irish bar with a difference.... we're actually Irish! Located just off Edinburgh's famous Grassmarket, Dropkick Murphy's gives you a real experience of what an Irish bar is meant to be. Live music at night, showing major sports on our big screens, and all out great craic assured - and we have free shows here through the Fringe from midday to 10pm, with the bar open until very late afterwards!
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, No wheelchair accessible toilet

Title: Titania – A Solo Cabaret
Description: An innovative re-imagining of A Midsummer Night's Dream, performed and created by renowned international theatre practitioner Anna-Helena McLean (formerly a principal performer with Poland’s legendary Gardzienice, Centre for Theatre Practices). This intoxicating performance promises an engaging, funny, sensual and participatory experience in which our much-loved queen of the night plays out events from her past, hosting nightly revels in an attempt to woo audiences off the path and back into the woods. A heady fusion of original music and vocal acrobatics, Titania is the Queen of the Faeries’ tale with an amplified twist.
Venue description: Summerhall presents engaging, challenging, high-quality theatre, dance, literature, visual art and music for people of all ages.  Our unique home in the former Dick Vet building of the University of Edinburgh offers atmospheric performance spaces, a buzzy courtyard and an onsite pub, the Royal Dick Bar, with something for everyone to explore, discover and enjoy - “an entire festival in its own right” The Guardian
Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café.
We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please do not hesitate to contact us by phone on 0845 874 3000 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

http://www.summerhall.co.uk/about/accessibility/. Title: Mark Stephenson: Amsterdam
Description: Mark Stephenson (Chortle Best Newcomer nominee, second New Act of the Year) brings you his new award nominated show (Leicester Comedy Festival Best Debut 2015) about the dystopian suburban childhood he suffered. There's nothing in here about a stag do or about the city of Amsterdam specifically; the title is a nod to the Dutch policy of euthanasia and the liberal freedom of the city. Enjoy! ‘Definitely a talent to watch’ **** (Time Out). ‘This is an auspicious beginning from an exhilarating new voice on the comedy circuit’ (Spoonfed.co.uk).
Venue description: The Banshee Labyrinth is a teeming pub that is said to be Scotland's most haunted pub. Regular comedy nights, karaoke and live music will keep you entertained until the wee small hours. Three performance spaces, three bars, one open from 12.30-05:00. 18+ only. www.thebansheelabyrinth.com

Title: Lazy Susan: Double Act
Description: The 2014 Foster’s Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Newcomer nominees return with their hotly anticipated second show. Lazy Susan stand side by side, sling on some wigs and take a few long shots at triumph. Watch as they make pacts, shake hands and get drunk on fiction. Character comedy that shoots straight from the hip: come get a slice of the zeal. As heard on BBC Radio 4's Newsjack and Sketchorama. 'Tender and ridiculous' (Guardian). 'Superb ... subtle performances and excellent writing' **** (List). 'Sparklingly funny' **** (Fest). **** (Time Out). **** (TheArtsDesk.com).
Venue description: Since 2000 the Pleasance Dome has been the hub of the now-famous Bristo Square, with the best comedy and theatre in 5 venues all under one roof. The legendary Pleasance atmosphere runs late in to the night.

Code: Stories Without Borders – Visions of Nicosia
Title: Stories Without Borders – Visions of Nicosia
Description: As Cyprus advances towards reunification after more than 40 years, Angus Reid and Dinda Fass make images of the divided capital city, Nicosia, and its two communities. They circulate the images as free postcards to gather responses, impressions and stories… the changing geographies of a long divided island.

Title: The Room: The Musical
Description: Oh, hai audience! We’ve got something for youuu! An original parody musical of the funniest disaster in cinematic history, Tommy Wiseau’s The Room, adapted by a BBC-award nominated writer. Loved by newcomers and hardcore fans alike. Tommy is a wonderful guy with the perfect life. But his sexy future-wife is sleeping... with his best friend! Will Tommy find out? Will disaster prevail? Will the other characters contribute anything? This show’s got everything. Romance! Atrocious dialogue! Bin accidents! Live musicians! Songs about cheesecake! ‘The best thing I have ever seen’ (Audience review). BYOS (bring your own spoons).
Artist: Two Spoons Productions / Laughing Horse Free Festival

Title: Having a Laugh with Julian Clary & David Roberts
Description: Mr and Mrs Bold are just like you and me: they live in a nice house, have jobs and love a bit of a giggle. There's one slight difference though - they're hyenas. Comedian, entertainer and novelist Julian Clary and illustrator David Roberts present their new book The Bolds. Come along for an event packed with hilarious jokes that'll have you laughing like a hyena!

Title: Christopher Fleet & Daniel MacCannell
Subtitle: Mapping Out New Stories
Description: Join the co-authors of Edinburgh: Mapping the City for an enlightening hour of discussion about why looking at the contours and marks of a map is the perfect place to start piecing together alternative versions of the past. Ideal for lovers of architectural history, town planning and cartography, this event is also for anyone intrigued by stories yet to be told. Chaired by Sheena McDonald.

Title: All's Well That Ends Well
Description: Helena is in love… Bertram is indifferent… And so begins one of theatre's greatest romances. Shakespeare offers a masterclass in the comic study of romantic ambition and class distinction as Helena eloquently plots and conspires using intelligence, resourcefulness and feminine wiles! All's Well That Ends Well shows strong women winning the war of the sexes as they use wit and wisdom against foolish and frivolous men. Set against a backdrop of the Second World War, this abridged production is filled with comedy amidst the battle of realising true love.
Venue description: Located right in the middle of it all on the Royal Mile, we present two theatres offering an array of new and established work, from theatre to musicals, panto, dance and physical work, a real feast for all . Hosted the winner of the NSDF best show award in 2014. Courtyard bar offers refreshments all day. Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Nick Harper
Description: Nick Harper: a rich acoustic/folk heritage (folk-legend Roy Harper's son!) recognised worldwide. ‘One of the finest guitarists of his generation, soaring vocals, epic songs’ (Mojo). 'Dylan for the iPod generation – Betjemen with a guitar' (Guitarist Magazine). 'The Acoustic Hendrix' (Guitar). Nick has also made recordings with Lana Del Rey, Newton Faulkner and Steven Wilson in the last year, but returns here – one man and a guitar – with a show that led the Herald to award Harper an EdFest Herald Angel award and exclaim, 'for my money the best singer/songwriter on the planet.' ***** (Herald).
Venue description: This stylish basement bar is Edinburgh's coolest, quintuple award-winning, year-round live music venue, with a crammed daily programme of multi-genre music and Fringe shows running all day, every day, from 13:00-05:00. Subtitle: Electricity, Music and Memory
Description: Born in Stirling, Montreal’s Sean Michaels won the Giller Prize (Canada’s Man Booker) for Us Conductors, a novel about electricity that tells the true story of Russian inventor and spy, Lev Termen. New Zealand’s Anna Smaill has penned The Chimes, set in a future London where music has replaced written words and memory is forbidden. Two debut novelists to keep an eye on.

Title: Lost in the Dust Exhibition
Description: Set against the dramatic and hauntingly beautiful backdrop of the South African landscape, these 15 works by Meyer offer a personal and compelling look into how war affects individual relationships, and captures the raw emotion of the people swept up in it. Meyer’s ancestors fought on both sides of the conflict. As such, the characters in this narrative series are drawn from Meyer’s imagination and purposefully ambiguous as to their British or Boer origin. His intention is for viewers to interpret the stories in their own way.
Warnings: Exhibition is Free to the Public. From 11th August to 20th August, 9:30 am – 4:30 pm. John Meyer will be making personal appearances at the venue on the first two days, times to be confirmed.

Title: Faye Treacy Worries
Description: Musical Comedy Awards Best Newcomer, Faye Treacy went to the Brit School of Performing Arts with Adele and Jessie J, and then studied the trombone at The Royal Academy of Music with no one interesting. Faye worries... a lot... about earning enough money to live from telling jokes and playing a dying instrument... relationships (well, one relationship in particular) homelessness, and avoiding it... her uber-dysfunctional family... and how damaging her half-arsed, part-time Nannying is.
